meta.spec_reference: CompuServe Graphics Interchange Format Version 89a (GIF89a), 31 July 1990: s.11 Header, s.13 Logical Screen Descriptor, s.15 Global Color Table, s.18 Graphic Control Extension, s.19 Comment Extension, s.20 Image Descriptor, s.22 Table-Based Image (LZW Minimum Code Size), s.23 Image Data, s.24 Local Color Table, s.25 Plain Text Extension, s.26 Application Extension, s.27 Trailer, Appendix F On-line LZW Compression; plus GIF87a (15 June 1987) for the alternate version string, and the de-facto Netscape 'NETSCAPE2.0' looping application extension. Template: 010 Editor GIF.bt v1.3 (2016-01-28) at templates_originals/gif-orig.bt.

schema_extensions.name: bit_layout
schema_extensions.where: constraints[*] entries for LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.*, IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.* and GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PACKEDFIELDS.*
schema_extensions.why: BitfieldLeftToRight() at line 63 makes the first declared bitfield the most significant bit of the packed byte. The rewrite step must know the exact bit positions to assemble that one byte correctly, and no key in the base schema expresses a bit position.

schema_extensions.name: tier
schema_extensions.why: Records whether an axis is a free Tier C field or a Tier A/B field that must still emit its entire legal set, so the rewrite step never pins a Tier B axis to one value while believing it is protecting diversity.

schema_extensions.name: must_emit_full_legal_set
schema_extensions.where: diversity_axes[*] entries whose tier is A or B
schema_extensions.why: must_remain_unconstrained cannot honestly be true for a Tier A/B axis; this key carries the actual instruction for those axes - vary across every legal value, never collapse to one.

schema_extensions.name: excluded_values
schema_extensions.why: That label's legal set is 'every byte value except four', which a free-text pattern alone cannot make machine-checkable; the explicit exclusion list keeps the enumeration complete without inventing a 252-element array.

schema_extensions.name: then.section / then.required / then.forbidden
schema_extensions.why: The base schema allows `then` to mark a whole section required or forbidden but names no keys for it; these three spell that out (used for the conditional Global and Local Color Tables).

schema_extensions.name: name / axis_detail_on
schema_extensions.why: Axes are one entry per field, as the base schema requires. `name` keeps a stable snake_case identifier for downstream tooling, and `axis_detail_on` records which field an entry details when its guidance was authored for a group of fields that must be varied together.

schema_extensions.name: variants
schema_extensions.where: diversity_axes[*], each {value, detail, frequency, reason, tier}
schema_extensions.why: Names the concrete shapes a field must take across a corpus, with an always/sometimes/rarely weighting, so the rewrite step protects real variety instead of guessing what free means for that field. Variant `tier` is the tier of the field the variant belongs to.

schema_extensions.name: diversity_budget
schema_extensions.why: States whether varying this axis costs file size and where that cost is charged (always structure.output_budget, never a cap on the field). This is the axis-side counterpart of the size-control rule and the reason no field may be narrowed to keep files small.

schema_extensions.name: how_varied
schema_extensions.why: The sampling instruction for this one field: which span to draw from, which values dominate, which pairings to honour. Without it the variants are a list with no distribution.

schema_extensions.name: notes
schema_extensions.why: Per-axis caveats with no other home, mirroring constraints[*].notes.

schema_extensions.name: length_prefix
schema_extensions.why: Added to the rule enumeration for DATASUBBLOCK.Size, whose value is the byte count of the data that follows it in the same sub-block. No base rule value expresses "this field is the length prefix of the bytes after it".

schema_extensions.name: then.field / then.tier / then.type / then.pattern / then.algorithm / then.covers / then.includes_self / then.endianness / then.depends_on
schema_extensions.why: `then` reuses the constraints[*] entry keys so a conditional rule can state a full typed constraint (pattern, calculated value, coverage) rather than only a value list, which is what the LZW code-size and table-length rules need.

schema_extensions.name: also_covers
schema_extensions.why: Lists constraint keys that this axis protects but that are not themselves axis entries, because they are the per-element sub-fields of the byte run the axis already names (RGB.R/G/B inside GLOBALCOLORTABLE.rgb). Keeps the rule "every Tier C unconstrained field appears in diversity_axes" checkable without duplicating an axis per array element.

meta.structure_note: GIF is a little-endian block stream: a 6-byte header, a 7-byte Logical Screen Descriptor with an optional Global Color Table, then an open-ended sequence of image and extension blocks each dispatched on its first one or two bytes (0x2C for a Table-Based Image, 0x21 plus a label for the five extension kinds), every image carrying an LZW-compressed pixel stream chunked into length-prefixed data sub-blocks, and a single 0x3B trailer byte; the format contains no CRC, checksum or Adler value anywhere, so the only opaque payload with required internal structure is the GIF LZW codestream at IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.

RGB.R.tier_rationale: A colour-table entry's red component is never validated by the template or by any decoder, so bounding it would only drain colour diversity out of the corpus without buying a single extra line of decoder coverage.
RGB.R.description: Red component of one Global/Local Color Table entry (an RGB triple); every byte value is legal.

RGB.G.tier_rationale: Palette green is unchecked data; constraining it costs the colour diversity that decoders feel through their colour-table copy and index-to-RGB conversion paths.
RGB.G.description: Green component of one Global/Local Color Table entry; every byte value is legal.

RGB.B.tier_rationale: Palette blue is unchecked data; like RGB.R and RGB.G it must stay free so generated files differ from one another.
RGB.B.description: Blue component of one Global/Local Color Table entry; every byte value is legal.

DATASUBBLOCK.Size.tier_rationale: This is the one-byte length prefix of a data sub-block; if it disagrees with the number of payload bytes that follow, the decoder's sub-block reassembly loop swallows the wrong bytes and every later structure - the LZW stream, the next extension, the 0x3B trailer - is misaligned, so the file is reported as corrupt before any useful work is done.
DATASUBBLOCK.Size.algorithm: byte count: Size equals the number of bytes in the DATASUBBLOCK.Data array that immediately follows it
DATASUBBLOCK.Size.covers: the DATASUBBLOCK.Data array directly after this byte (exactly Size bytes)
DATASUBBLOCK.Size.description: Length prefix of one data sub-block; any value 1..255 is legal inside a sequence, while 0 is not a sub-block at all - it ends the sequence and is consumed by DATASUBBLOCKS.BlockTerminator.
DATASUBBLOCK.Size.notes: The template lookaheads this byte at line 44 (local UBYTE size = ReadUByte(FTell())) and again at line 50 after each block, looping at line 45 while it is non-zero; the only literal it is compared against is 0. How a payload is split into sub-blocks (one 255-byte block plus a remainder, or many small ones) is free diversity - only the per-block Size/Data agreement is pinned.

DATASUBBLOCK.Data.tier_rationale: The container itself says nothing about these bytes - their meaning is fixed by the enclosing structure - so the only rule that belongs here is the length agreement with DATASUBBLOCK.Size; bounding the content or the per-block length would delete the sub-block chunking diversity that the decoder's reassembly loop feels.
DATASUBBLOCK.Data.description: Size raw payload bytes of one data sub-block; validity is defined by whatever encloses the sequence (see IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks, which is Tier A payload_wellformedness because it must hold an LZW codestream).
DATASUBBLOCK.Data.notes: Do not confuse container with content: DATASUBBLOCK.Size (Tier A) fixes the length of this array, the bytes inside are free everywhere except in the IMAGEDATA case. `size` on line 48 is the template's local variable, not a field written to the file.

DATASUBBLOCKS.BlockTerminator.tier_rationale: The zero-length block terminator is what ends every data sub-block sequence; without it the decoder keeps reading length-prefixed blocks past the end of the payload, misparses the following block and reports truncated or corrupt data instead of decoding the image.
DATASUBBLOCKS.BlockTerminator.description: Block terminator ending a data sub-block sequence: a length prefix of 0 with no data bytes following it.
DATASUBBLOCKS.BlockTerminator.notes: Line 45 loops `while (size != 0)` on the byte lookahead at lines 44 and 50, so the byte that ends the loop is exactly the byte this field reads - the terminator is not an extra byte after the last sub-block, it is the rejected length prefix. GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.BlockTerminator (line 152) is a separate, equally mandatory 0x00.

GIFHEADER.Signature.tier_rationale: The template's own guard at line 78 rejects anything but "GIF" and stops the parse, and every real decoder tests these three bytes first - a wrong signature means the decoder exits at byte 0 having executed almost nothing.
GIFHEADER.Signature.description: Three-byte GIF signature at offset 0, always the ASCII string 'GIF'.
GIFHEADER.Signature.notes: Line 11 records the ID bytes '47 49 46 //GIF'; on failure line 80 emits Warning("File is not a valid GIF. Template stopped.") and line 81 returns -1. No lookahead call is involved - the field is read directly and then compared.

GIFHEADER.Version.tier_rationale: The template guards only the Signature (line 78) and never compares Version, and decoders accept any three characters here - they use the string only to decide which GIF89a-only extensions to honour - so a wrong value does not make the decoder refuse the file and the field is an enumeration, not a gate.
GIFHEADER.Version.description: Three-character version string immediately after the signature; '87a' denotes the 1987 format without extensions, '89a' the 1989 format that defines the Graphic Control, Comment, Plain Text and Application extensions and transparency.
GIFHEADER.Version.notes: '89a' is preferred because the extensions this template parses (lines 136-190) are GIF89a features and a strict decoder told '87a' may skip them, costing depth; '87a' is still legal and still must be emitted, since it drives the decoder's version-dependent branches. Completeness is exhaustive: GIF87a and GIF89a are the only two versions ever published by CompuServe; both must be emitted.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.Width.tier_rationale: The logical screen width is never validated - images may extend past it and decoders clip rather than refuse - so capping it would collapse the canvas-size diversity that drives allocation size, clipping arithmetic and row-stride handling.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.Width.description: Width of the logical screen (canvas) in pixels; any ushort value is syntactically legal, including 0 and values smaller than the images it contains.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.Width.notes: LittleEndian() at line 30 applies to every multi-byte field in this format. This field must not be narrowed to keep files small - output size is controlled by the DATA output_budget in `structure`.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.Height.tier_rationale: The logical screen height is never validated and does not bound any image; pinning it would remove the tall/short-canvas variation that changes decoder allocation and clipping paths for no depth at all.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.Height.description: Height of the logical screen (canvas) in pixels; any ushort value is syntactically legal.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.Height.notes: Total file size is bounded by the DATA output_budget, never by this field.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Glo.tier_rationale: One bit whose complete legal set is {0,1}; it is a section-presence switch rather than a gate - a wrong value never makes the decoder refuse the file, it only decides whether a Global Color Table follows - so it is enumerated over both values, never pinned to one.
value_names: Global Color Table present immediately after the Logical Screen Descriptor
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Glo.description: MSB of the Logical Screen Descriptor packed byte; 1 means a Global Color Table of 3*2^(SizeOfGlobalColorTable+1) bytes follows the descriptor.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Glo.bit_layout: bit 7 of the packed byte (BitfieldLeftToRight() at line 63): packed = (GlobalColorTableFlag<<7) | (ColorResolution<<4) | (SortFlag<<3) | SizeOfGlobalColorTable
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Glo.notes: 1 is preferred because with no colour table there is nothing for pixel indices to refer to and most decoders abandon the frame early; 0 is legal, must still be emitted, and exercises the no-GCT path plus the BackgroundColorIndex rule. Template line 88: `if (LogicalScreenDescriptor.PackedFields.GlobalColorTableFlag == 1) {`. Completeness is exhaustive: a 1-bit field has exactly two legal values.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Col.tier_rationale: Three purely informational bits (bits of colour resolution minus 1) that no decoder branches on and that have no named enumeration; recording a legal set here would buy nothing and could be read as a narrowing, so it stays free.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Col.description: Number of bits of colour resolution per primary colour, minus 1, as declared in the Logical Screen Descriptor packed byte; informational only.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Col.notes: An author is tempted to tie this to SizeOfGlobalColorTable for plausibility; GIF89a does not require it and decoders ignore any mismatch, so leaving it free is correct.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Sor.tier_rationale: One bit, so the complete legal set is {0,1}; decoders store it as informational and never refuse a file over it, which makes it a flag enumeration rather than a Tier A gate.
value_names: Global Color Table is not sorted
Global Color Table is sorted by decreasing importance
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Sor.description: Indicates whether the Global Color Table entries are sorted; no decoder takes a parse-depth decision on it.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Sor.notes: Completeness is exhaustive: a 1-bit field has exactly two legal values.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Siz.tier_rationale: All eight values of this 3-bit selector are legal and none makes a decoder refuse the file, but each one observably changes the parse - the Global Color Table length the template derives at lines 92-96, and with it the canonical LZW code size - so this is an enumeration whose complete set must be emitted. Pinning it (for example to keep the colour table small so files stay short) is exactly the size-for-diversity trade the output_budget exists to prevent, and it would freeze the decoder's colour-table loop and the code-size basis at one value.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Siz.description: N such that the Global Color Table holds 2^(N+1) entries (3*2^(N+1) bytes): 0 means 2 entries, 7 means 256 entries.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Siz.notes: The derived byte count is Tier A on GLOBALCOLORTABLE.rgb; the selector itself ranges over all eight values so generated files carry 2-, 4-, 8- ... 256-entry tables and the decoder's table-reading loop takes different iteration counts, and every value must appear across a corpus. Ignored by decoders when GlobalColorTableFlag is 0, but still emitted and still varied in both cases. Completeness is exhaustive: a 3-bit field has exactly eight legal values, each selecting a different table length from 2 to 256 entries; no value may be dropped, including 7, whose 768-byte table is the most expensive to emit.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.BackgroundColorI.tier_rationale: A colour-table index that no decoder validates - out-of-range values are ignored or clamped, never rejected - so bounding it to the table size would delete the decoder's out-of-range handling path and cost diversity for nothing.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.BackgroundColorI.description: Index of the background colour in the Global Color Table, used to clear the canvas between frames; any byte value is syntactically legal.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.BackgroundColorI.notes: GIF89a says the field should be 0 when no Global Color Table is present; that is recorded as an advisory dependency and deliberately does not narrow this field's span.

LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.PixelAspectRatio.tier_rationale: An informational byte from which a decoder computes (PixelAspectRatio+15)/64 only to report a ratio; no value causes refusal, so leaving it free costs nothing and adds header variation.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.PixelAspectRatio.description: Aspect ratio of a pixel: 0 means 'not specified', otherwise the ratio is (PixelAspectRatio+15)/64.
LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.PixelAspectRatio.notes: Tempting to restrict to the near-1.0 ratios a real encoder would pick; that is a narrowing with no depth behind it, so it is not recorded.

GLOBALCOLORTABLE.rgb.tier_rationale: The template allocates this array from SizeOfGlobalColorTable (lines 92-96) and reads exactly that many RGB triples; if the emitted byte count disagrees, every following structure - the first image descriptor, its LZW stream, the trailer - is misaligned and the decoder reports corrupt data before rendering anything.
GLOBALCOLORTABLE.rgb.algorithm: element count derived from a 3-bit selector: entries = 2^(SizeOfGlobalColorTable+1), bytes = 3 * entries (the loop at lines 93-95 doubles a local `size` once per increment of i from 0 to N inclusive)
GLOBALCOLORTABLE.rgb.covers: the entire GLOBALCOLORTABLE structure immediately following the 7-byte Logical Screen Descriptor (3 * 2^(SizeOfGlobalColorTable+1) bytes, present only when GlobalColorTableFlag is 1)
GLOBALCOLORTABLE.rgb.description: Array of RGB triples; present only when GlobalColorTableFlag is 1, and then exactly 2^(N+1) entries long.
GLOBALCOLORTABLE.rgb.notes: The element count is Tier A and is derived from the free 3-bit selector; the R/G/B values inside each element stay Tier C. `local int size` (line 92) is computed at parse time and is never written to the file.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageSeperator.tier_rationale: The template dispatches the whole data-block loop on this byte (line 104) and real decoders require 0x2C, 0x21 or 0x3B at a block boundary; any other value makes the decoder report an unexpected byte and stop before the image data is reached.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageSeperator.description: Image separator byte that introduces a Table-Based Image block.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageSeperator.notes: Spelled 'ImageSeperator' in the template (line 107) - keep that identifier verbatim. Line 104 is `if (ReadUByte(FTell()) == 0x2C) {`, the call site that decides the branch.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageLeftPosition.tier_rationale: An offset into the logical screen that decoders clip rather than validate; bounding it would remove the sub-image placement paths (offset clipping, partial-canvas update, off-canvas images) from the corpus.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageLeftPosition.description: X offset of this image inside the logical screen; may be 0, may exceed the logical screen width, and is never a reason for a decoder to refuse the file.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageLeftPosition.notes: The logical screen dimensions do not bound this field: GIF89a permits an image to extend past the canvas and decoders clip.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageTopPosition.tier_rationale: Same as ImageLeftPosition for the vertical axis - clipped, never validated - so capping it would only make every generated frame land in the same place.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageTopPosition.description: Y offset of this image inside the logical screen; any ushort value is syntactically legal.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageWidth.tier_rationale: This is the field a previous run narrowed to {1,2,4,8} and lost 1.7 coverage points for: no decoder validates it, it sets the pixel count the LZW stream must deliver, and shrinking it to suit a handful of precomputed payloads destroys row-stride, clipping and buffer-size diversity while buying zero depth - the payload must be derived from this value, never the reverse.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageWidth.description: Width of this image in pixels; any ushort value is syntactically legal, including values wider than the logical screen and including 0 (which decoders handle as an empty frame).
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageWidth.notes: Paired with IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks through payload_wellformedness.derives_from: whatever value this field takes, emit ImageWidth*ImageHeight pixel codes into the LZW stream computed from it. File size is controlled by the DATA output_budget in `structure`, not by this field, and no minimum, maximum or value set may be attached to it.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageHeight.tier_rationale: The declared number of pixel rows, never validated by the template or by decoders; together with ImageWidth it drives the LZW decode loop bound and the de-interlacing pass arithmetic, so restricting it to powers of two would collapse the very diversity that moves the decoder through different row-handling code.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageHeight.description: Height of this image in pixels; any ushort value is syntactically legal, including values taller than the logical screen.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageHeight.notes: Paired with IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks through derives_from: the LZW stream is built to deliver ImageWidth*ImageHeight indices. Odd, prime, very tall and very wide values are all legitimate and all reach different decoder code; no cap may be recorded here.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.LocalColorT.tier_rationale: One bit whose complete legal set is {0,1}; it selects whether a Local Color Table is present and which table the image's indices refer to, and a wrong value never makes the decoder refuse the file - it is a section switch, so both values must be emitted.
value_names: no Local Color Table; the image uses the Global Color Table
Local Color Table present immediately after the Image Descriptor and used in place of the Global Color Table
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.LocalColorT.description: MSB of the Image Descriptor packed byte; 1 means 3*2^(SizeOfLocalColorTable+1) bytes of Local Color Table sit between the descriptor and the image data.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.LocalColorT.bit_layout: bit 7 of the packed byte: packed = (LocalColorTableFlag<<7) | (InterlaceFlag<<6) | (SortFlag<<5) | (Reserved<<3) | SizeOfLocalColorTable
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.LocalColorT.notes: Both values are deep paths: 1 adds a colour-table read and the table-override logic, 0 keeps the global table live. Template line 120: `if (ImageDescriptor.PackedFields.LocalColorTableFlag == 1) {`. Completeness is exhaustive: a 1-bit field has exactly two legal values.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.InterlaceFl.tier_rationale: One bit, complete legal set {0,1}; a wrong value never causes refusal, it changes the order in which rows are consumed - and that is a large, distinct region of decoder code, so both values must be emitted.
value_names: image is not interlaced (rows in sequential order)
image is interlaced (rows delivered in four passes: 0,8,16...; 4,12,20...; 2,6,10...; 1,3,5...)
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.InterlaceFl.description: Selects the row order of the image's pixel data and therefore the order the LZW stream must deliver indices in.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.InterlaceFl.notes: This flag is a payload-shape dependency, not a value restriction: when it is 1 the LZW stream must be emitted in interlace pass order (see dependencies and IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks). Never pin it to 0 to avoid implementing the pass ordering. Completeness is exhaustive: a 1-bit field has exactly two legal values.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.SortFlag.tier_rationale: One bit, complete legal set {0,1}; informational only and never a reason for refusal, so it is enumerated over both values rather than pinned.
value_names: Local Color Table is not sorted
Local Color Table is sorted by decreasing importance
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.SortFlag.description: Indicates whether the Local Color Table is sorted; only meaningful when LocalColorTableFlag is 1.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.SortFlag.notes: Completeness is exhaustive: a 1-bit field has exactly two legal values.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Reserved.tier_rationale: Two bits the template names Reserved and no decoder inspects - GIF89a reserves them for future use rather than requiring zero, and decoders mask the packed byte without validating it - so zeroing them removes free variation for no depth.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Reserved.description: Two reserved bits in the Image Descriptor packed byte; every value 0-3 parses identically.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.Reserved.notes: Close call against Tier A fixed_value 0: rejected because the template has no Assert or comparison on these bits and no conforming decoder refuses a file over them.

IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.SizeOfLocal.tier_rationale: All eight values of this 3-bit selector are legal and none makes a decoder refuse the file, but each one observably changes the parse - the Local Color Table length the template derives at lines 124-128, and with it the canonical LZW code size for this image - so this is an enumeration whose complete set must be emitted. Pinning it to keep tables small would freeze the table-reading loop and the code-size basis, which is the size-for-diversity trade this schema forbids.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.SizeOfLocal.description: N such that the Local Color Table holds 2^(N+1) entries (3*2^(N+1) bytes): 0 means 2 entries, 7 means 256 entries.
IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.SizeOfLocal.notes: The derived byte count is Tier A on LOCALCOLORTABLE.rgb; all eight selector values must appear across a corpus, ideally within a single file so one animation mixes palette sizes. Decoders read it whenever LocalColorTableFlag is 1 and ignore it otherwise, but it is emitted and varied in both cases. Completeness is exhaustive: a 3-bit field has exactly eight legal values, each selecting a different table length from 2 to 256 entries; no value may be dropped.

LOCALCOLORTABLE.rgb.tier_rationale: The template sizes this array from SizeOfLocalColorTable (lines 124-128) and reads exactly that many RGB triples before the image data; a wrong byte count puts the LZW minimum code size at the wrong offset and the decoder fails on the image data instead of decoding it.
LOCALCOLORTABLE.rgb.algorithm: element count derived from a 3-bit selector: entries = 2^(SizeOfLocalColorTable+1), bytes = 3 * entries (the loop at lines 125-127 doubles a local `size` once per increment of i from 0 to N inclusive)
LOCALCOLORTABLE.rgb.covers: the entire LOCALCOLORTABLE structure immediately following the 10-byte Image Descriptor (3 * 2^(SizeOfLocalColorTable+1) bytes, present only when LocalColorTableFlag is 1)
LOCALCOLORTABLE.rgb.description: Array of RGB triples; present only when LocalColorTableFlag is 1, then exactly 2^(N+1) entries long, and used in place of the Global Color Table for this image only.
LOCALCOLORTABLE.rgb.notes: The element count is Tier A and derived from the free selector; the RGB values stay Tier C. `local int size` (line 124) is a parse-time variable and is never written to the file.

IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize.tier_rationale: This byte parameterises the LZW decoder that follows: outside 2..8 the initial code width and the CLEAR/EOI codes cannot be modelled within GIF's 12-bit limit, and decoders reject the image at this byte - giflib's DGifDecompressLine/LZWReadCode and Firefox's nsGIFDecoder2 both bail out before delivering a single scanline.
IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize.pattern: integer 2 <= LZWMinimumCodeSize <= 8; with N = LZWMinimumCodeSize the initial code width is N+1 bits, CLEAR = 2^N, EOI = 2^N + 1 and the first free dictionary slot is 2^N + 2
IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize.description: Minimum code size in bits of the LZW-compressed image data that immediately follows; canonically the number of bits needed to index the image's active colour table, but any value 2..8 is decoder-acceptable.
IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize.notes: Every value in 2..8 must be emitted - each gives the LZW decoder a different starting dictionary and code width, which is real coverage. Do not pin it to one value in order to reuse a precomputed payload: build the payload from the value instead (see IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.generation_strategy). Values 0, 1 and 9..255 are Tier A evil and must never be generated; 9..12 are outside GIF89a even though a 12-bit-wide codestream is representable.

IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.tier_rationale: This is the opaque byte run the template declares as DATASUBBLOCKS without ever saying what is inside it, and it must be a real GIF LZW codestream: with random bytes the decoder's LZW stage hits a code outside its current dictionary and aborts before delivering any scanline, so all pixel placement, de-interlacing, transparency and disposal code stays unexecuted.
IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.description: The LZW-compressed pixel-index stream of one image, carried as a sequence of length-prefixed data sub-blocks terminated by 0x00, immediately following the one-byte LZWMinimumCodeSize.
IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.codec: GIF LZW - variable-width-code Lempel-Ziv as defined in GIF89a Appendix F (On-line LZW Compression) and GIF87a Appendix C, carried in the GIF data-sub-block framing of GIF89a s.23 (Image Data)
IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.must_produce: Byte-exact structure: (1) zero or more data sub-blocks, each [Size][Size payload bytes] with Size in 1..255, whose concatenated payload bytes form ONE continuous bit stream; (2) that bit stream is a sequence of variable-width codes packed LSB-first into bytes - the least significant bit of the first code goes into bit 0 of the first byte, codes straddle byte boundaries, and bytes fill from bit 0 upward; (3) with N = LZWMinimumCodeSize the code width starts at N+1 bits, CLEAR = 2^N, EOI = 2^N+1, and the first free dictionary slot is 2^N+2; (4) the stream begins with a CLEAR code, continues with codes that are always valid for the decoder's current dictionary (a single-character literal code below 2^N, or a code already present in the table), and ends with a CLEAR followed by EOI; (5) the unused high bits of the final byte are zero-filled; (6) the sequence ends with one 0x00 block terminator (DATASUBBLOCKS.BlockTerminator); (7) between the first CLEAR and the final EOI the stream must deliver at least ImageWidth*ImageHeight pixel codes, laid out row-major, or in GIF four-pass interlace order when InterlaceFlag is 1.
IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.decoder_gate: giflib (ImageMagick, libgd, gifsicle, most CLI decoders): DGifDecompressLine() -> LZWReadCode() reads a code greater than the current running dictionary size, returns GIF_ERROR / D_GIF_ERR_DATA_TOO_BIG ('Error reading image data'), and the caller receives no scanlines at all - the header, descriptor and colour table are parsed and then the frame dies. Firefox nsGIFDecoder2: the invalid code triggers PostDataError() and the frame is abandoned at its first row. Chrome/Skia GIFImageDecoder: the frame is flagged as incomplete and no pixels are handed to the compositor. In all three, everything downstream of the LZW decoder - pixel placement, four-pass de-interlacing, transparent-index handling, disposal-method compositing, canvas blitting - is unreachable for a random-byte payload. This is the single highest-value constraint in the file: it is the GIF analogue of a real zlib stream in PNG IDAT.
IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.generation_strategy:
Simplest correct construction - the LZW equivalent of a deflate stored block, a 'clear-code run' that never grows the dictionary and therefore never has to widen the codes:
 1. Read the chosen dimensions and code size: W = IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageWidth, H = IMAGEDESCRIPTOR.ImageHeight, N = IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize (2..8), width = N+1 bits, CLEAR = 1<<N, EOI = CLEAR+1.
 2. Open a bit writer that appends codes low-bit-first: to write code c of `width` bits, for b in 0..width-1 emit bit (c>>b)&1 into the next free bit position of the output byte stream, filling each byte from bit 0 upward and starting a new byte after bit 7 is used.
 3. Write CLEAR.
 4. Write W*H literal pixel codes, one per pixel, each a free value in 0..(1<<N)-1 (constant, random, gradient, noise, runs - all legal; see content_is_free). Every `limit` literals, where limit = (1<<N) - 3, write another CLEAR before continuing: this resets the decoder's dictionary so the code width provably never exceeds N+1 and no table-growth bookkeeping is needed. (After a CLEAR the next free slot is CLEAR+2 and each subsequent code adds one slot, so a width increase would need (1<<(N+1)) - (CLEAR+2) = (1<<N) - 2 literals; stopping at (1<<N) - 3 leaves a margin of one under both the standard rule and the 'early change' convention some decoders accept.)
 5. Write CLEAR, then EOI, then zero-fill the final partial byte.
 6. Split the resulting byte buffer into sub-blocks of at most 255 bytes, prefixing each with its length byte, and append a single 0x00 terminator. The split points are free - one 255-byte block plus a remainder, or many small blocks - and the decoder's reassembly loop feels the difference.
 7. If IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.InterlaceFlag is 1, feed step 4 in GIF interlace order (rows 0,8,16,...; then 4,12,20,...; then 2,6,10,...; then 1,3,5,..., each pass skipping rows already emitted and short images omitting empty passes); if 0, feed plain top-to-bottom row order.
 8. Never invert this derivation: never choose or narrow ImageWidth/ImageHeight/LZWMinimumCodeSize to fit a precomputed payload. Compute the payload from the freely chosen values every time.
IMAGEDATA.DataSubBlocks.notes: The pixel index values inside the stream are unconstrained apart from being below 2^N so that they decode as single-character literals (indices at or above 2^N would collide with CLEAR, EOI and dictionary codes). The number and sizes of the data sub-blocks are also free, bounded only by the DATA output_budget. The active colour table has 2^(SizeOf...+1) entries (local when LocalColorTableFlag is 1, else global), so choosing N canonically makes every emitted index a valid colour; decoders tolerate indices beyond the table and take their out-of-range path. Decoders ignore surplus codes once W*H pixels have been produced and pad a stream that ends early, but a stream that produces exactly W*H pixels reaches the deepest paths.

GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.ExtensionIntrodu.tier_rationale: At a block boundary a decoder accepts only 0x2C, 0x21 or 0x3B; this byte is the extension introducer that the template matches as the low byte of the 16-bit lookahead 0xF921 at line 136, and any other value makes the decoder report unexpected data and stop.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.ExtensionIntrodu.description: Extension introducer byte, the first byte of every GIF extension block.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.ExtensionIntrodu.notes: Line 136 is `} else if (ReadUShort(FTell()) == 0xF921) {`. LittleEndian() (line 30) makes 0xF921 the byte pair 0x21 then 0xF9 on disk, so this single lookahead pins both the introducer and the label. 0xF921 = 63777 decimal.

GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.GraphicControlLa.tier_rationale: The label selects which extension the decoder dispatches to; a wrong value routes the block to the unknown-extension skip path or, in strict decoders, to a data error - either way the disposal, delay and transparency handling this extension exists to exercise is never reached.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.GraphicControlLa.description: Graphic Control Extension label byte, immediately after the 0x21 extension introducer.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.GraphicControlLa.notes: Same call site as the introducer: ReadUShort(FTell()) == 0xF921 pins the byte pair {0x21, 0xF9} in that on-disk order.

GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.tier_rationale: The decoder uses this length to skip or read exactly the extension's data and to find the block terminator that follows; a wrong value desynchronises the stream, so the next block - often the image itself - is misparsed and the file is rejected.
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.algorithm: byte count of the fixed-size data that follows this length byte inside GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.covers: GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PACKEDFIELDS (1 byte) + DelayTime (2 bytes) + TransparentColorIndex (1 byte) = 4 bytes, i.e. every byte of GraphicControlSubBlock after BlockSize and before GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.BlockTerminator
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.description: Length of the Graphic Control Extension's data block; constant 4 (0x04) because the sub-block layout is fixed by GIF89a s.18.
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.notes: Expressed as a byte count rather than a literal so the rewrite step derives it from the fields it actually emits; the covered region is fixed-size, so the result is always 4. This extension is NOT a generic DATASUBBLOCKS sequence - it has its own explicit terminator at line 152.

GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.tier_rationale: Three bits named Reserved that the template never compares and no decoder validates - decoders mask the packed byte and branch only on DisposalMethod, UserInputFlag and TransparentColorFlag - so forcing them to zero removes free variation without buying depth.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.description: Three reserved bits in the Graphic Control Extension packed byte; every value 0-7 parses identically.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.bit_layout: bits 7-5 of the packed byte: packed = (Reserved<<5) | (DisposalMethod<<2) | (UserInputFlag<<1) | TransparentColorFlag
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.notes: Close call against Tier A fixed_value 0 (GIF89a says 'reserved for future use, should be 0'); rejected because nothing in the template or in conforming decoders refuses a non-zero value.

GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.tier_rationale: A 3-bit enumeration whose eight values select different canvas-compositing behaviour; none of them makes the decoder refuse the file, so all eight are legal and must be emitted - each is a separate branch in the decoder's frame-disposal code.
value_names: do not dispose (leave graphic in place)
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.description: How the canvas is treated after this graphic is rendered; 2 and 3 force the decoder to save or clear the previous frame region.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.notes: 1, 2 and 3 are preferred because they drive the deepest compositing code (leave-in-place, restore-to-background using LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR.BackgroundColorIndex, and restore-to-previous requiring a saved frame buffer); 0 and 4-7 are still emitted because they take the normalise/ignore branches. Completeness is exhaustive: a 3-bit field has exactly eight legal values; GIF89a names 0-3 and leaves 4-7 to be defined, but decoders accept and normalise them (Firefox clamps above 3, giflib stores them), so they are legal and must not be dropped.

GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.tier_rationale: One bit, complete legal set {0,1}; it never causes refusal - decoders store it for the renderer's input-wait logic - so both values are recorded and neither may be dropped.
value_names: do not wait for user input
wait for user input before continuing (bounded by DelayTime)
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.description: Whether the renderer should wait for user input before advancing to the next frame.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.notes: Completeness is exhaustive: a 1-bit field has exactly two legal values.

GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.tier_rationale: One bit, complete legal set {0,1}; it switches the decoder's transparent-index handling on and off and never causes refusal, so both values must be emitted to reach both branches.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.description: Whether GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.TransparentColorIndex names a transparent palette entry for the following graphic.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION_DATASUBBLOCK_PAC.notes: 1 is the interesting half - it makes the decoder test every decoded pixel index against the transparent index during compositing - but 0 must be emitted just as often because it is the default path in real files. Completeness is exhaustive: a 1-bit field has exactly two legal values.

GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.DelayTime.tier_rationale: A duration in hundredths of a second that decoders never validate; bounding it would make every animation frame identical in timing and remove the zero-delay, huge-delay and normal-delay paths from the corpus.
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.DelayTime.description: Delay before the next frame is displayed, in hundredths of a second, little-endian; any ushort value is legal, including 0.
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.DelayTime.notes: Interacts with UserInputFlag only semantically (an input wait is bounded by the delay); no constraint follows from that.

GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.TransparentColorI.tier_rationale: A palette index that decoders never validate - an out-of-range value simply never matches a decoded pixel, and in-range versus out-of-range are both real decoder paths - so restricting it to the colour table size would delete the out-of-range branch and cost diversity.
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.TransparentColorI.description: Index of the transparent colour in the following graphic's active colour table; any byte value is syntactically legal.
GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.TransparentColorI.notes: Read only when TransparentColorFlag is 1 (see dependencies); the field stays free in both cases. Pairing it with pixel indices that the LZW stream actually emits is a generator choice, not a format constraint.

GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.BlockTerminator.tier_rationale: The extension's data block is length-prefixed by GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK.BlockSize and must be closed by this 0x00 byte; if it is missing or wrong the decoder is left one byte out of step and the following image descriptor is misparsed, ending the frame in a data error.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.BlockTerminator.description: Block terminator closing the Graphic Control Extension, immediately after the 4 data bytes.
GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.BlockTerminator.notes: This extension does not use the DATASUBBLOCKS structure, so this terminator is a separate mandatory byte and not the loop-exit byte of line 45.

COMMENTEXTENSION.ExtensionIntroducer.tier_rationale: At a block boundary a decoder accepts only 0x2C, 0x21 or 0x3B; this byte is the 0x21 that the template matches as the low byte of the lookahead 0xFE21 at line 154, and any other value ends the parse in an unexpected-byte error.
COMMENTEXTENSION.ExtensionIntroducer.description: Extension introducer byte of a Comment Extension.
COMMENTEXTENSION.ExtensionIntroducer.notes: Line 154 is `} else if (ReadUShort(FTell()) == 0xFE21) {`; little-endian, so 0xFE21 = 65057 decimal is the byte pair 0x21 then 0xFE.

COMMENTEXTENSION.CommentLabel.tier_rationale: The label routes the block to the comment-skip routine; a wrong value sends it down the unknown-extension path or, in strict decoders, to a data error, so the intended comment-handling code is never reached.
COMMENTEXTENSION.CommentLabel.description: Comment Extension label byte, immediately after the 0x21 extension introducer.

COMMENTEXTENSION.CommentData.tier_rationale: Free-form text the decoder reads only to skip it; its length and content are unchecked, so bounding either would remove a cheap, high-volume diversity axis (short comments, many sub-blocks, long multi-block comments) for no depth.
COMMENTEXTENSION.CommentData.description: A DATASUBBLOCKS sequence of arbitrary text bytes; only the sub-block framing (DATASUBBLOCK.Size agreement and the 0x00 DATASUBBLOCKS.BlockTerminator) is constrained.
COMMENTEXTENSION.CommentData.notes: An empty comment (a lone 0x00 terminator) and a multi-hundred-byte comment split across several 255-byte sub-blocks both parse; emitting both ends of that span exercises the decoder's skip loop differently.

PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.ExtensionIntroducer.tier_rationale: The 0x21 introducer is the low byte of the lookahead 0x0121 at line 161; at a block boundary anything other than 0x2C, 0x21 or 0x3B makes the decoder report unexpected data and stop.
PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.ExtensionIntroducer.description: Extension introducer byte of a Plain Text Extension.
PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.ExtensionIntroducer.notes: Line 161 is `} else if (ReadUShort(FTell()) == 0x0121) {`; little-endian, so 0x0121 = 289 decimal is the byte pair 0x21 then 0x01.

PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.PlainTextLabel.tier_rationale: The label routes the block to the plain-text handler; a wrong value sends it to the unknown-extension skip path instead, so the text-grid parsing this block exists to exercise never runs.
PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.PlainTextLabel.description: Plain Text Extension label byte, immediately after the 0x21 extension introducer.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.tier_rationale: The decoder uses this length to read exactly the text-grid parameters and to locate the data sub-blocks that follow; a wrong value desynchronises the stream so the text data and every later block are misparsed.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.algorithm: byte count of the fixed-size data that follows this length byte inside PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.covers: TextGridLeftPosition (2) + TextGridTopPosition (2) + TextGridWidth (2) + TextGridHeight (2) + CharacterCellWidth (1) + CharacterCellHeight (1) + TextForegroundColorIndex (1) + TextBackgroundColorIndex (1) = 12 bytes, i.e. every byte of PlainTextSubBlock after BlockSize and before PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.PlainTextData
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.description: Length of the Plain Text Extension's parameter block; constant 12 (0x0C) because the layout is fixed by GIF89a s.25.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.notes: Recorded as a byte count so the rewrite step derives it from the fields it emits; the covered region is fixed-size, so it is always 12.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridLeftPosition.tier_rationale: A grid offset that decoders clip or ignore (most do not render plain text at all); bounding it would remove placement diversity without touching any validation.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridLeftPosition.description: X offset of the plain-text grid inside the logical screen; any ushort value is legal.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridTopPosition.tier_rationale: A grid offset that is never validated; free variation here costs nothing and keeps generated files distinct.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridTopPosition.description: Y offset of the plain-text grid inside the logical screen; any ushort value is legal.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridWidth.tier_rationale: A grid dimension that no decoder validates - implementations that render plain text divide it by the character cell width and clip the result - so capping it would remove the loop-bound and divide-by-cell diversity this extension can offer.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridWidth.description: Width of the plain-text grid in pixels; any ushort value is legal, including 0 and values wider than the logical screen.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridWidth.notes: Together with TextGridHeight, CharacterCellWidth and CharacterCellHeight it determines how many character cells a decoder that renders plain text would lay out; that is a derived quantity, not a reason to narrow this field.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridHeight.tier_rationale: A grid dimension that no decoder validates; like TextGridWidth it must stay free so generated files differ and so cell-count loops in text-rendering decoders see different bounds.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextGridHeight.description: Height of the plain-text grid in pixels; any ushort value is legal, including 0.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.CharacterCellWidth.tier_rationale: A cell dimension no decoder validates; even the divide-by-zero worry is not a Tier A case because conforming decoders that render plain text guard the division and those that do not simply never run this code - capping it would remove the divisor variation that changes cell counts and loop bounds.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.CharacterCellWidth.description: Width of one character cell in pixels; any byte value is legal, including 0.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.CharacterCellWidth.notes: Close call against Tier A: rejected. No Assert or comparison exists in the template and no conforming decoder refuses the file for a 0 or oversized cell; the risk noted here is a crash in a non-guarding implementation, which is fuzzing value, not a validity rule.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.CharacterCellHeight.tier_rationale: A cell dimension that is never validated; free variation changes the number of text rows a rendering decoder computes, which is diversity rather than risk.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.CharacterCellHeight.description: Height of one character cell in pixels; any byte value is legal, including 0.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextForegroundColorInd.tier_rationale: A palette index that no decoder validates - out-of-range values are ignored or clamped - so restricting it to the colour table size would delete an out-of-range branch for no depth.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextForegroundColorInd.description: Index of the text foreground colour in the active colour table; any byte value is legal.

PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextBackgroundColorInd.tier_rationale: A palette index that no decoder validates; it stays free for the same reason as TextForegroundColorIndex.
PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK.TextBackgroundColorInd.description: Index of the text background colour in the active colour table; any byte value is legal.

PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.PlainTextData.tier_rationale: Free-form character bytes that a decoder reads only to place or skip them; their content and total length are unchecked, so bounding either would remove a cheap diversity axis for no depth.
PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.PlainTextData.description: A DATASUBBLOCKS sequence holding the text characters; only the sub-block framing is constrained (DATASUBBLOCK.Size agreement plus the 0x00 terminator).
PLAINTEXTEXTENTION.PlainTextData.notes: GIF89a does not require the character count to match the grid capacity (TextGridWidth/CharacterCellWidth * TextGridHeight/CharacterCellHeight); implementations that render plain text simply wrap or truncate. No dependency is recorded, so both under-full and over-full text are legal emissions.

APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ExtensionIntroducer.tier_rationale: The 0x21 introducer is the low byte of the lookahead 0xFF21 at line 179; at a block boundary a decoder accepts only 0x2C, 0x21 or 0x3B and anything else stops the parse.
APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ExtensionIntroducer.description: Extension introducer byte of an Application Extension.
APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ExtensionIntroducer.notes: Line 179 is `} else if (ReadUShort(FTell()) == 0xFF21) {`; little-endian, so 0xFF21 = 65313 decimal is the byte pair 0x21 then 0xFF.

APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ApplicationLabel.tier_rationale: The label routes the block to the application-extension handler; a wrong value sends it down the unknown-extension skip path, so the identifier/authentication parsing never runs.
APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ApplicationLabel.description: Application Extension label byte, immediately after the 0x21 extension introducer.

APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.tier_rationale: The decoder reads exactly this many bytes as the application identifier plus authentication code before the data sub-blocks begin; a wrong value desynchronises the stream and the rest of the file is misparsed.
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.algorithm: byte count of the fixed-size data that follows this length byte inside APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.covers: ApplicationIdentifier (8 bytes) + ApplicationAuthenticationCode (3 bytes) = 11 bytes, i.e. every byte of ApplicationSubBlock after BlockSize and before APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ApplicationData
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.description: Length of the application identification block; constant 11 (0x0B) because the layout is fixed by GIF89a s.26.
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.BlockSize.notes: Recorded as a byte count so the rewrite step derives it from the two fixed-size char arrays it emits; the covered region never varies, so it is always 11.

APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.ApplicationIdentifie.tier_rationale: Eight free ASCII bytes that a decoder compares against known identifiers but never rejects on mismatch - an unknown identifier just means the extension is skipped - so pinning it would delete the unknown-application path and every identifier-specific branch that a varied corpus could reach.
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.ApplicationIdentifie.description: Eight bytes identifying the application that created the extension data; any bytes are legal, printable or not.
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.ApplicationIdentifie.notes: The widely deployed value is 'NETSCAPE' paired with the authentication code '2.0' (the de-facto looping extension); emitting it sometimes reaches the decoder's loop-count branch. That is one interesting value, not a restriction - the full 8-byte space stays free.

APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.ApplicationAuthentic.tier_rationale: Three free bytes that authenticators compare but decoders never reject on; pinning them would remove the mismatch branch that makes a decoder fall back to generic application-data handling.
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.ApplicationAuthentic.description: Three bytes of application-specific authentication data following the identifier; any bytes are legal.
APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK.ApplicationAuthentic.notes: '2.0' is the de-facto value that goes with the 'NETSCAPE' identifier; it is one interesting value, not a restriction.

APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ApplicationData.tier_rationale: Application-private bytes whose content the format defines only per application; a decoder skips whatever it does not recognise, so bounding the content or the sub-block layout would delete the skip-loop diversity this extension provides for no depth.
APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ApplicationData.description: A DATASUBBLOCKS sequence of application-defined bytes; only the sub-block framing is constrained.
APPLICATIONEXTENTION.ApplicationData.notes: For the de-facto Netscape looping extension the first sub-block is [0x03][0x01][loop count as a little-endian ushort]; emitting that shape sometimes reaches a decoder's loop-count branch (see dependencies). It is optional: arbitrary bytes and an empty sequence (a lone 0x00 terminator) are equally legal.

UNDEFINEDDATA.ExtensionIntroducer.tier_rationale: This branch is reached by exclusion, but a generator must still emit 0x21 here: at a block boundary a conforming decoder accepts only 0x2C, 0x21 or 0x3B, so any other leading byte makes it report unexpected data and stop before the remaining blocks are parsed - it is a gate even though the template treats the struct as a catch-all.
UNDEFINEDDATA.ExtensionIntroducer.description: Extension introducer byte of an extension whose label is not one of the four the template recognises; the block is then [0x21][unknown label][data sub-blocks][0x00].
UNDEFINEDDATA.ExtensionIntroducer.notes: Close call against Tier C: the template's else branch (line 191) would parse any byte here, and its own comment says 21. Tier A wins because the objective is a file a real decoder keeps reading - an unknown extension with 0x21 is skipped cleanly and parsing continues, while a stray non-0x21 byte ends the stream. Emitting unknown extensions is valuable: it drives the decoder's extension-skip and resynchronise code.

UNDEFINEDDATA.Label.tier_rationale: An extension label no decoder validates - unrecognised labels are skipped, never rejected - so it is an enumeration, not a gate; but the four labels the template dispatches elsewhere must not be repeated here or the block stops being an unknown extension.
UNDEFINEDDATA.Label.pattern: any byte value 0x00-0xFF except 0x01, 0xF9, 0xFE and 0xFF, each of which is parsed by its own dedicated struct (PLAINTEXTEXTENTION, GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION, COMMENTEXTENSION, APPLICATIONEXTENTION)
UNDEFINEDDATA.Label.description: Label of an unrecognised extension; 252 byte values are legal here and all of them reach the decoder's generic extension-skip routine.
UNDEFINEDDATA.Label.notes: The four ReadUShort call sites at lines 136, 154, 161 and 179 reject 0xF921, 0xFE21, 0x0121 and 0xFF21 respectively; anything else with a leading 0x21 falls through to line 191. The template's comment '// F9' on line 195 is stale documentation of the example label, not a required value - 0xF9 is in fact excluded here because it is the Graphic Control Extension. The full legal set is deliberately expressed as a pattern plus an exclusion list rather than a 252-element array; no value in that set may be dropped.

UNDEFINEDDATA.DataSubBlocks.tier_rationale: Payload of an unrecognised extension, which by definition no decoder interprets - it only walks the sub-block framing to skip it - so content and length are free and bounding them would delete skip-loop diversity.
UNDEFINEDDATA.DataSubBlocks.description: A DATASUBBLOCKS sequence of arbitrary bytes; only the sub-block framing (DATASUBBLOCK.Size agreement plus the 0x00 terminator) is constrained, and that framing is what lets the decoder resynchronise on the next block.
UNDEFINEDDATA.DataSubBlocks.notes: An empty sequence (a lone 0x00) and a long multi-sub-block sequence both parse; vary both.

TRAILER.GIFTrailer.tier_rationale: The template's data loop at line 102 exits only on this byte and real decoders treat 0x3B as the end-of-stream marker; without it the decoder reports a truncated file and, in strict implementations, discards the last frame instead of finishing it.
TRAILER.GIFTrailer.description: GIF trailer byte, the final byte of the file.
TRAILER.GIFTrailer.notes: Line 102 is `while (ReadUByte(FTell()) != 0x3B) {` - the loop condition is a lookahead on this exact byte, and line 203 then consumes it. Nothing may follow it.

then.covers: the Global Color Table immediately after the 7-byte Logical Screen Descriptor

dependencies.description: When the Global Color Table flag is set, the table must be present and exactly 3*2^(N+1) bytes long, because both the template's local `size` (lines 92-95) and every decoder's colour-table read are derived from N.

When the flag is 0 no colour-table bytes may be emitted: the byte after the Logical Screen Descriptor must begin a <Data> block (0x21, 0x2C or 0x3B), and inserting table bytes there misaligns the entire stream.

GIF89a says the background colour index should be 0 when there is no Global Color Table, because there is no entry for it to name; this is advisory only - decoders ignore the index in that case - so the field keeps its full free span and is NOT narrowed to 0.

then.covers: the Local Color Table between the 10-byte Image Descriptor and IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize

dependencies.description: When the Local Color Table flag is set the table must be present, exactly 3*2^(N+1) bytes long, and contiguous with the image descriptor on one side and the image data on the other.

When the flag is 0 no local table bytes may be emitted: IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize must be the very next byte after the Image Descriptor packed field, otherwise the LZW code size is read from the wrong offset and the frame dies.

then.pattern: canonical value max(2, SizeOfLocalColorTable + 1); any value 2..8 remains decoder-acceptable

dependencies.description: With a Local Color Table the canonical minimum code size is one more than the table's size selector (floor 2), because that is the number of bits needed to index the table; this is a derivation from a free field, not a narrowing - the LZW payload is then built from whatever code size results.

then.pattern: canonical value max(2, SizeOfGlobalColorTable + 1) when a Global Color Table is present, else 2; any value 2..8 remains decoder-acceptable

dependencies.description: Without a local table the image's indices refer to the Global Color Table, so the canonical code size derives from SizeOfGlobalColorTable (floor 2); with no colour table at all the floor of 2 applies. Again a derivation from free fields, never a narrowing of them.

then.algorithm: the LZW codestream must deliver ImageWidth * ImageHeight pixel-index codes between the initial CLEAR and the final EOI

dependencies.description: The declared dimensions decide how many pixels the LZW stream must produce; the stream is computed from ImageWidth and ImageHeight, and those two fields are never narrowed to fit a precomputed payload. This is the rule the previous GIF run inverted, at a cost of 1.7 coverage points.

then.algorithm: pixel codes emitted in GIF four-pass interlace order: rows 0,8,16,...; then 4,12,20,...; then 2,6,10,...; then 1,3,5,..., skipping rows already emitted and omitting empty passes

dependencies.description: An interlaced image's LZW stream carries its rows in interlace pass order, not top-to-bottom order; the decoder's de-interlacer then places them, so the payload shape follows the flag.

then.algorithm: pixel codes emitted row-major, top row first, ImageWidth codes per row

dependencies.description: A non-interlaced image's LZW stream carries its rows in plain sequential order.

With the flag set the index is interpreted against the following graphic's active colour table (local if present, else global): a value inside the table makes matching pixels transparent during compositing, a value outside it exercises the decoder's no-match / out-of-range handling. Both are decodable, so the field stays completely free; when the flag is 0 the index is ignored entirely and is equally free.

Disposal method 2 (restore to background) is the case in which the background colour index becomes semantically live, because the decoder clears the frame's region to that colour before the next frame; the index is still never validated, so it stays free - the dependency is recorded so the rewrite step varies the two together rather than pinning either.

For the de-facto Netscape looping extension (identifier 'NETSCAPE', authentication code '2.0') the first data sub-block conventionally holds [0x03][0x01][loop count as a little-endian ushort], which is what makes a decoder take its loop-count branch; this is an optional shape, not a requirement - the field's content remains free for every other identifier and for any sub-block layout.

structure.subject: GIFHEADER
structure.detail: The 6-byte header (Signature 'GIF' + Version) must start at file offset 0 with no preamble, byte-order mark or padding before it.
structure.description: The GIF data stream begins with its header, which the template reads first at line 77 and guards at line 78.
structure.output_budget: n/a - single fixed 6-byte head element; not a repeating structure.
structure.generation_note: Emit as a fixed head element: bytes 47 49 46 followed by the version string, then immediately the Logical Screen Descriptor.

structure.subject: LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR
structure.detail: Exactly one 7-byte Logical Screen Descriptor (Width, Height, PackedFields, BackgroundColorIndex, PixelAspectRatio) must immediately follow the header at offset 6.
structure.description: The grammar at template line 23 is <Logical Screen> ::= Logical Screen Descriptor [Global Color Table], and the template reads the descriptor unconditionally at line 86.
structure.output_budget: n/a - single fixed 7-byte element; not a repeating structure.
structure.generation_note: Emit as a fixed head element directly after the header; its Width/Height are free Tier C values and must not be capped.

structure.subject: GLOBALCOLORTABLE
structure.detail: When LOGICALSCREENDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.GlobalColorTableFlag is 1, the 3*2^(SizeOfGlobalColorTable+1)-byte Global Color Table must immediately follow the descriptor at offset 13, before any <Data> block; when the flag is 0 no table bytes may appear there.
structure.description: The optional colour table sits between the Logical Screen Descriptor and the first data block, exactly where the template reads it (lines 88-97).
structure.output_budget: Derived, not free: 3*2^(N+1) bytes for N = SizeOfGlobalColorTable, i.e. between 6 and 768 bytes. The table length follows from a free 3-bit field and is never capped to save bytes; the cost is accounted for inside the DATA budget rationale below.
structure.generation_note: Emit immediately after the descriptor as a fixed-length array of RGB triples whose count is computed from the freely chosen size selector; the RGB values themselves are free.

structure.subject: DATA
structure.detail: struct DATA repeats zero or more times (template line 102: `while (ReadUByte(FTell()) != 0x3B)`); each iteration is exactly one block - a Table-Based Image, a Graphic Control Extension, a Comment Extension, a Plain Text Extension, an Application Extension or an unknown extension - and the loop ends only on the 0x3B trailer byte.
structure.description: The open-ended middle of the grammar, <Data>*, is where nearly all of a GIF's bytes and nearly all of its decoder-branch diversity live.
structure.output_budget: Total budget for the whole <Data> region: 65536 bytes (64 KiB) of running output measured from file offset 0. The generator keeps a running byte counter, and before starting each new block it checks the counter; once starting another block would exceed the budget it stops and emits the 1-byte Trailer. Recommended floor for depth: at least one complete Table-Based Image block (descriptor + optional local colour table + LZWMinimumCodeSize + LZW sub-blocks + terminator) and at least one extension of a different kind, so every generated file reaches the LZW decoder. Rationale: 64 KiB carries several full frames (a 64x64 image costs roughly 1.5-5 KiB with the clear-code-run strategy) plus many extensions, stays inside every decoder's input buffering, and is far beyond the point where extra bytes add coverage. This budget is the ONLY size-control mechanism in this document: no field anywhere has been capped, ranged or valued to keep files small.
structure.generation_note: Emit as a repeated array of blocks bounded by output_budget: choose a block kind per iteration (mixing images and extensions), build it completely and well-formed, add its byte length to the running counter, and stop when the next block would exceed the budget - then emit the Trailer. Never satisfy the budget by shrinking ImageWidth, ImageHeight, the colour-table selectors or DelayTime.

structure.subject: TRAILER
structure.detail: The single byte 0x3B must be the last byte of the file; the data loop exits only on it (line 102) and the template consumes it at line 203.
structure.description: GIF's trailer terminates the data stream and marks the end of the file.
structure.output_budget: n/a - single fixed 1-byte tail element; not a repeating structure.
structure.generation_note: Emit as a fixed tail element after the DATA region, once the output_budget is reached or the chosen block sequence is complete.

structure.subject: block dispatch inside DATA
structure.detail: At every position inside DATA exactly one block form is emitted, selected by the first one or two bytes: 0x2C -> IMAGEDESCRIPTOR [+ LOCALCOLORTABLE] + IMAGEDATA; 0x21 0xF9 -> GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION; 0x21 0xFE -> COMMENTEXTENSION; 0x21 0x01 -> PLAINTEXTEXTENTION; 0x21 0xFF -> APPLICATIONEXTENTION; 0x21 <any other label> -> UNDEFINEDDATA; 0x3B -> end of DATA (TRAILER).
structure.description: The template's if/else-if chain at lines 104-198 is a strict dispatch on these prefixes, and decoders dispatch the same way.
structure.output_budget: Shared: every block drawn from this dispatch counts against the single DATA output_budget above; there is no per-kind sub-budget, so the mix of block kinds is free.
structure.generation_note: Pick one prefix per iteration and emit that block's complete, well-formed body; a stray byte that matches none of the prefixes aborts a real decoder, so never emit one outside the UNDEFINEDDATA form.

structure.subject: LOCALCOLORTABLE
structure.detail: When IMAGEDESCRIPTOR_PACKEDFIELDS.LocalColorTableFlag is 1, the 3*2^(SizeOfLocalColorTable+1)-byte Local Color Table must sit immediately between the 10-byte Image Descriptor and IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize, per template line 131; when the flag is 0 nothing may be inserted there.
structure.description: A per-image colour table that overrides the Global Color Table for the indices decoded from that image's LZW stream.
structure.output_budget: Derived, not free: 3*2^(N+1) bytes for N = SizeOfLocalColorTable, i.e. between 6 and 768 bytes per image, charged to the DATA output_budget like every other per-block cost.
structure.generation_note: Emit directly after the image descriptor's packed field and before the LZW minimum code size; length follows from the free 3-bit selector.

structure.subject: DATASUBBLOCK
structure.detail: Every data sub-block is [DATASUBBLOCK.Size][Size payload bytes], with Size in 0x01-0xFF (0x00 is never a length here, it is the terminator); the Size byte is included in the byte budget of the region it lives in.
structure.description: GIF's universal sub-block framing, used by comment, plain-text, application, unknown-extension and image data alike (template line 19, loop at lines 42-47).
structure.output_budget: Per sub-block cost: Size + 1 bytes, charged to the enclosing region's budget (for IMAGEDATA that is the DATA output_budget). The 255-byte Size cap is a hard format boundary and NOT a soft budget: to emit N bytes of LZW data use ceil(N/255) sub-blocks.
structure.generation_note: Chunk the payload into sub-blocks of at most 255 bytes, prefixing each chunk with its exact byte length; never write a Size byte that disagrees with the number of payload bytes actually emitted.

structure.subject: DATASUBBLOCKS termination
structure.detail: Every DATASUBBLOCKS sequence ends with DATASUBBLOCKS.BlockTerminator = 0x00, i.e. a zero-length sub-block, which is what lets the loop at lines 42-47 (`do { ... } while (DATASUBBLOCK.Size != 0x00)`) exit.
structure.description: The terminator is the only way a decoder knows a sub-block sequence is complete; omitting it makes the decoder read the next block's leading byte as a length and desynchronise the stream.
structure.output_budget: 1 byte per sequence, charged to the enclosing region's budget.
structure.generation_note: Always append a single 0x00 after the last non-zero-length sub-block; an empty sequence is legal and is just that one byte.

structure.subject: IMAGEDATA
structure.detail: IMAGEDATA must begin with LZWMinimumCodeSize immediately after the Image Descriptor (and after the Local Color Table if present) and end with the DATASUBBLOCKS terminator; the template reads it at lines 132-134.
structure.description: The image's compressed pixel data, framed so the decoder knows where the LZW stream starts and stops.
structure.output_budget: The LZW sub-blocks inside are charged to the DATA output_budget; with the clear-code-run strategy a small image (16x16) costs a few hundred bytes and a 64x64 image roughly 1.5-5 KiB depending on the code size.
structure.generation_note: Emit code size, then the LZW sub-blocks, then the terminator; never reorder these three parts.

structure.subject: GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK
structure.detail: GRAPHICCONTROLSUBBLOCK is [BlockSize=0x04][PackedFields][DelayTime][TransparentColorIndex], with BlockSize prefixing the 4 data bytes that follow it (template line 115).
structure.description: The Graphic Control Extension carries its four parameters as a single length-prefixed data block rather than as a DATASUBBLOCKS sequence.
structure.output_budget: Fixed 5 bytes per extension, charged to the DATA output_budget.
structure.generation_note: Emit 0x04 then the packed byte, the little-endian delay and the transparent index; the length must be recomputed if the layout were ever extended, which GIF89a does not allow.

structure.subject: GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION closure
structure.detail: GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION is terminated by its own GRAPHICCONTROLEXTENSION.BlockTerminator = 0x00 immediately after the 4-byte data block; it does not use DATASUBBLOCKS and therefore has no second terminator.
structure.description: Without this byte the decoder is left one byte out of step and misparses the following Image Descriptor as extension data.
structure.output_budget: 1 byte per extension, charged to the DATA output_budget.
structure.generation_note: Emit exactly one 0x00 after TransparentColorIndex; a Graphic Control Extension is 8 bytes in total.

structure.subject: PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK
structure.detail: PLAINTEXTSUBBLOCK is [BlockSize=0x0C][eight text-grid parameter fields totalling 12 bytes], immediately followed by the PlainTextData sub-block sequence (template lines 166-179).
structure.description: The Plain Text Extension's parameter block is length-prefixed and fixed at 12 bytes.
structure.output_budget: Fixed 13 bytes for the parameter block plus whatever PlainTextData costs, charged to the DATA output_budget.
structure.generation_note: Emit 0x0C, then the four little-endian ushorts and four bytes, then the text data sub-blocks and their terminator.

structure.subject: APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK
structure.detail: APPLICATIONSUBBLOCK is [BlockSize=0x0B][ApplicationIdentifier (8 bytes)][ApplicationAuthenticationCode (3 bytes)], immediately followed by the ApplicationData sub-block sequence (template lines 184-191).
structure.description: The Application Extension's identification block is length-prefixed and fixed at 11 bytes.
structure.output_budget: Fixed 12 bytes for the identification block plus whatever ApplicationData costs, charged to the DATA output_budget.
structure.generation_note: Emit 0x0B, then 8 identifier bytes and 3 authentication bytes, then the application data sub-blocks and their terminator.

diversity_axes.why: A 1-bit flag whose complete legal set is {0,1}; both must be emitted because they change whether 3*2^(N+1) table bytes exist at all, and dropping one removes a real parse branch for no size saving.
