diversity_axes.name: local_color_table_flag
diversity_axes.why: Both values are legal and both must be emitted: 1 inserts a per-image table between the descriptor and the code size, 0 leaves the LZW byte immediately after the packed field. Dropping either removes a real parse branch.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0 makes the decoder read LZWMinimumCodeSize as the very next byte; 1 makes it first read 3*2^(N+1) table bytes and use them instead of the global table for this image indices (giflib swaps the local ColorMap in for the frame).

variants.detail: no local table; the image's indices refer to the Global Color Table
variants.reason: The common layout for single-palette files and for most animation frames.

variants.detail: 3*2^(SizeOfLocalColorTable+1) bytes of RGB triples sit between the image descriptor and LZWMinimumCodeSize
variants.reason: Per-frame palettes, which switch the decoder's active-table lookup and make the canonical code size derive from the local selector instead.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential: value 1 adds 6-768 bytes per image depending on local_color_table_size, charged to the DATA output_budget. Both values must appear; the flag is never pinned to 0 to save bytes.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose per image, not per file, so a single animation can mix frames with and without local tables.
diversity_axes.notes: When 0, LZWMinimumCodeSize must be the very next byte after the packed field - see dependencies.

diversity_axes.name: size_of_local_color_table
diversity_axes.why: All eight selectors are legal and each changes the local table length; the full set must appear across a corpus, ideally mixed within one file so a single animation carries different palette sizes per frame.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The local table-reading loop iteration count, the palette used to validate this image decoded indices and the canonical code size for this frame.

variants.detail: 2 colours, 6-byte local table
variants.reason: Smallest legal local palette; forces the code-size floor of 2 and 1-bit indices.
Every intermediate selector exercises the 2^(N+1) sizing arithmetic and a different index bit-width in the LZW decoder.

variants.detail: 256 colours, 768-byte local table
variants.reason: The dominant real-world choice, and the only one that reaches the full 8-bit index path.

variants.detail: a local selector deliberately different from SizeOfGlobalColorTable, e.g. global 7 with local 1
variants.reason: Proves the decoder switches the active table and code-size basis per image rather than reusing the global one.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential: the local table costs 3*2^(N+1) bytes per image that has one, from 6 to 768, charged to the DATA output_budget. All eight selectors must appear across a corpus; the budget is met by using fewer images or smaller dimensions, never by dropping selectors.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Weight N=7 most heavily, draw every value 0-7 regularly, and vary it per image so one file can mix palette sizes.
diversity_axes.notes: Only meaningful when LocalColorTableFlag is 1; when the flag is 0 the three bits are still emitted and decoders ignore the value.

diversity_axes.name: interlace_flag
diversity_axes.why: Both values must be emitted, and must_remain_unconstrained is true in the sense that matters here: the whole legal set {0,1} is emitted and neither value may be dropped or pinned, because the LZW payload row order is derived from it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0 decodes rows top-to-bottom; 1 switches the decoder to the four-pass interlace order (rows 0,8,16..., then 4,12,20..., then 2,6,10..., then 1,3,5...) with a different destination-row stride per pass, and short images skip whole passes.

variants.detail: sequential rows: the LZW stream carries row 0, row 1, ... in order
variants.reason: The common layout and the simpler decoder path.

variants.detail: four-pass interlace: rows 0,8,16,...; then 4,12,20,...; then 2,6,10,...; then 1,3,5,... with empty passes omitted
variants.reason: Drives the decoder's de-interlacer, including its row-advance tables and its handling of images too short for some passes (a 3-row image has empty passes 2-4).

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a for the flag itself (one bit); consequential through the payload, because the same pixel count must be emitted in a different row order. No extra bytes, so both values are free to emit as often as wanted.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose per image; a corpus should hold roughly as many interlaced as sequential images, and should combine interlace with tiny heights (1, 2, 3, 5 rows) to reach the empty-pass arithmetic.
diversity_axes.notes: This flag is a derives_from input of the LZW payload constraint: it changes emission order, not the number of pixel codes.

diversity_axes.name: reserved
diversity_axes.why: Two reserved bits nobody checks; they are free diversity inside the packed byte and must not be pinned to 0 just because the specification calls them reserved.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: None - conforming decoders mask them out. Varying them proves the mask is applied and adds packed-byte diversity at zero cost.

variants.detail: all three reserved bits clear, as real encoders write
variants.reason: The conventional value; keeps the packed byte looking like every file a decoder has seen.

variants.detail: any value 1-7 in bits 7-5 of the packed byte
variants.reason: Reaches whatever a decoder does with reserved bits it was told to ignore - most mask them, some do not.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - three bits inside an already-emitted byte; zero extra bytes and no size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 0 most of the time and a nonzero value in a minority of images.
diversity_axes.notes: The same axis shape applies to the Graphic Control Extension's reserved bits (graphic_control_reserved); both are recorded because they are independent fields in different structs.

diversity_axes.name: sort_flag
diversity_axes.why: A 1-bit flag whose complete legal set is {0,1}; both must be emitted, and pinning it to 0 would remove the sorted-palette branch for no size saving.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 1 tells the decoder the Global Color Table is sorted by decreasing importance, which affects colour-quantisation and index-priority handling in decoders that honour it; 0 is the default path.

variants.detail: Global Color Table not sorted
variants.reason: The default; palette order carries no importance ranking.

variants.detail: Global Color Table sorted by decreasing importance
variants.reason: Reaches the index-priority and colour-quantisation handling of decoders that honour the flag.

variants.detail: claims sorting the emitted table does not have
variants.reason: Nothing validates the claim, so a lying flag is legal and reaches the decoder path that trusts it.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - one bit each inside already-emitted packed bytes; no size consequence, so all four combinations are free to emit.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of the local sort flag so all four global/local combinations appear across a corpus; the table bytes vary on the colour-table content axes.
diversity_axes.notes: must_emit_full_legal_set: a 1-bit flag whose complete legal set is {0,1}; neither value may be dropped, and the flag is never checked against the table it describes.

diversity_axes.name: imagedescriptor_packedfields_sort_flag
diversity_axes.why: The same complete 1-bit legal set as the screen-descriptor sort flag, applied to the Local Color Table; both values must be emitted per image.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 1 marks the local table as sorted, which decoders that honour the flag use when deciding which entries to keep; 0 is the default path.

variants.detail: Local Color Table not sorted
variants.reason: The default for a per-frame palette.

variants.detail: Local Color Table sorted by decreasing importance
variants.reason: Reaches the same priority handling as the global flag, applied to this frame.

variants.detail: claims sorting the emitted local table does not have
variants.reason: Legal and unvalidated; per-frame sort claims let one file carry both behaviours.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - one bit each inside already-emitted packed bytes; no size consequence, so all four combinations are free to emit.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently per image so all four global/local sort-flag combinations appear; one file can carry both behaviours across its frames.
diversity_axes.notes: must_emit_full_legal_set: a 1-bit flag whose complete legal set is {0,1}; neither value may be dropped, and it applies to the local table of the image that carries it.

diversity_axes.name: rgb
diversity_axes.why: The table LENGTH is Tier A and derived from the selector; the CONTENT is completely free and must vary on every file. Listed because it is the largest free byte run in the header and an author might be tempted to fill it with a fixed ramp to keep files comparable.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Every decoded index becomes one of these triples, so the content drives the compositing, transparency-comparison and colour-caching paths; all-zero, saturated-corner, duplicate-entry and random tables each reach different code.

variants.detail: every RGB triple 00 00 00
variants.reason: Cheapest table content; makes every palette entry identical, which reaches the decoder's degenerate-colour paths.

variants.detail: entry i = (i,i,i) or an evenly spaced luminance ramp
variants.reason: Sorted-looking palettes that interact meaningfully with SortFlag and with transparency indices.

variants.detail: uniform random bytes per channel
variants.reason: Maximises distinct decoder inputs for free and never repeats across a corpus.

variants.detail: all 0xFF, and single-channel saturations like FF 00 00 / 00 FF 00 / 00 00 FF
variants.reason: Boundary values in each channel, plus the primaries that compositing and transparency code paths treat specially.

variants.detail: several entries with identical RGB values
variants.reason: Exercises palette-deduplication and index-to-colour caching in decoders.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential only through table length, which is already fixed by the size selector (3*2^(N+1) bytes) and charged to the DATA output_budget; the CONTENT of those bytes is free and costs nothing extra, so it should vary on every single file.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Fill the table with random bytes by default and substitute the structured variants (ramp, corners, duplicates) on a minority of files; vary it on every file.
diversity_axes.notes: Table length is never a diversity choice here - it is derived from the selector. Only the bytes inside it vary. Also covers the per-element constraints RGB.R, RGB.G and RGB.B: the same RGB struct is what LOCALCOLORTABLE.rgb holds, and every byte of every triple in either table is free.

diversity_axes.name: localcolortable_rgb
diversity_axes.why: Free content for the same reason as the global table, and free per image, so one file can carry several different palettes; the length is derived, the bytes are not.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Overrides the global table for this image indices, so its content decides which colour-lookup and transparency-comparison branches run for that frame.

variants.detail: every RGB triple 00 00 00
variants.reason: Cheapest table content; makes every palette entry identical, which reaches the decoder's degenerate-colour paths.

variants.detail: entry i = (i,i,i) or an evenly spaced luminance ramp
variants.reason: Sorted-looking palettes that interact meaningfully with SortFlag and with transparency indices.

variants.detail: uniform random bytes per channel
variants.reason: Maximises distinct decoder inputs for free and never repeats across a corpus.

variants.detail: all 0xFF, and single-channel saturations like FF 00 00 / 00 FF 00 / 00 00 FF
variants.reason: Boundary values in each channel, plus the primaries that compositing and transparency code paths treat specially.

variants.detail: several entries with identical RGB values
variants.reason: Exercises palette-deduplication and index-to-colour caching in decoders.

diversity_axes.how_varied: Fill each local table with random bytes by default, substitute the structured variants on a minority of images, and let one file carry several different palettes.
diversity_axes.notes: Table length is never a diversity choice here - it is derived from the selector. Only the bytes inside it vary.

diversity_axes.name: lzw_minimum_code_size
diversity_axes.why: Listed with must_remain_unconstrained true in the sense that matters: it varies freely inside its Tier A legal set 2..8 and is never pinned to one value, because the LZW code widths, CLEAR and EOI values are derived from it. It appears in derives_from precisely so the rewrite step builds the payload from this byte instead of narrowing this byte to fit a precomputed payload.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Sets the initial code width (N+1 bits), CLEAR = 2^N, EOI = 2^N+1 and the first free dictionary slot, so every value gives the LZW decoder a different starting dictionary, a different width-growth schedule and a different index-validity bound; values outside 2..8 make giflib and Firefox refuse the image before any scanline is delivered.

variants.detail: the floor: clear and end-of-information codes at 4 and 5, first code width 3 bits
variants.reason: The minimum a GIF LZW decoder must support, and the value that pairs with 2- and 4-colour tables.

variants.detail: 8-colour palette basis
variants.reason: Low-colour images.

variants.detail: 16-colour palette basis
variants.reason: Common low-colour GIF size.

variants.detail: 32-colour palette basis
variants.reason: Mid palette.

variants.detail: 64-colour palette basis
variants.reason: Mid-large palette.

variants.detail: 128-colour palette basis
variants.reason: Large palette.

variants.detail: 256-colour palette basis; the top of the legal span
variants.reason: The dominant real-world value and the only one that reaches the full 8-bit index path and the widest code growth.

variants.detail: a code size smaller or larger than the active table's selector implies, e.g. 2 with a 256-colour table, or 8 with a 2-colour table
variants.reason: Decoders derive their initial code width from this byte, not from the table, so a mismatch reaches the index-out-of-range and width-growth paths that matched files never touch.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential through the payload: a smaller code size produces a shorter LZW stream for the same image, a larger one a longer stream. That cost or saving is charged to the DATA output_budget; all seven legal values plus the mismatched pairings must appear in a corpus.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Derive the canonical value from the active colour table's size selector most of the time, and deliberately deviate on a minority of images. The LZW payload is always built from whatever value is finally emitted.
diversity_axes.notes: This is a derives_from field of the LZW payload constraint: it fixes the initial code width, the CLEAR and EOI code numbers, and the point at which the width grows.

diversity_axes.name: data_sub_blocks
diversity_axes.why: The LZW payload itself. Its framing and code structure are Tier A, but its contents are free (content_is_free), so it is a diversity axis of a different kind: the chunking of the stream into sub-blocks and the pixel codes inside it vary per file at no depth cost.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The sub-block reassembly loop iteration count, the LZW dictionary-growth path (literal-only clear-code runs versus table-growing streams), the code-width increase point, and the row or interlace delivery order.

variants.detail: a leading CLEAR, then CLEAR codes repeated until the pixel budget is met, then a final CLEAR and EOI; every literal index is 0
variants.reason: The default strategy: it produces a well-formed stream of the exact required pixel count in a few hundred bytes whatever the image size, because CLEAR resets the dictionary before any code can grow past the initial width. It reaches the decoder's clear-handling and dictionary-reset paths on every single file.

variants.detail: CLEAR, then width*height literal codes all equal to one index, then EOI, letting the dictionary fill and the code width grow to 12 bits
variants.reason: Drives the code-width growth arithmetic and the 4096-entry dictionary ceiling, which the clear-code run deliberately avoids.

variants.detail: CLEAR, then literals cycling through every index the active colour table defines (0..entries-1), then EOI
variants.reason: Touches every palette entry, so transparency-index matching, out-of-range index handling and colour lookups all see live data.

variants.detail: CLEAR, then literals followed by progressively longer table codes so the dictionary is filled near capacity, then EOI
variants.reason: The deepest LZW decoder path: table-code resolution, deferred-clear handling and the full/overflow boundary at 4096 entries.

variants.detail: CLEAR, a run of literals, CLEAR, another run, CLEAR, ... , EOI
variants.reason: Exercises repeated dictionary resets mid-stream, which is where decoders disagree about code width after a clear.

variants.detail: any of the shapes above with pixel codes emitted in four-pass interlace order when InterlaceFlag is 1
variants.reason: The payload must follow the flag or the de-interlacer places rows wrongly; combining shapes with interlace doubles the branch coverage of the row-advance tables.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: This axis is the main consumer of the DATA output_budget: the clear-code run costs about (initial code width + 1) bits per pixel plus sub-block framing - roughly 1.2 bytes per pixel at code size 8 (9-bit CLEAR codes) and 0.4 bytes per pixel at code size 2 (3-bit CLEAR codes), so a 64x64 image lands near 1.5-5 KiB - while flat-literal and dictionary-heavy streams cost several times that for the same image once the code width grows. The generator picks the shape and the image size together so the running byte counter stays under the budget, and it never reduces the number of pixel codes below width*height to fit - an under-delivered stream is a malformed file, not a small one.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose a shape per image, weighted so clear-code run dominates and the deeper shapes appear regularly; always honour InterlaceFlag when ordering the codes and always terminate with EOI.
diversity_axes.notes: Every variant must emit CLEAR first, deliver exactly ImageWidth*ImageHeight pixel-index codes, and end with EOI; the sub-block framing on top of the bitstream is varied separately by subblock_framing_shape.

diversity_axes.name: size
diversity_axes.why: A derived length whose derivation has many legal shapes: the same payload may be split into one 255-byte block plus a remainder, or into many small blocks. Every legal length 1..255 must appear across a corpus; only 0 is illegal here, because it is the terminator.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The sub-block loop iteration count and the per-iteration copy length; 1-byte, 254-byte and 255-byte blocks exercise the reassembly buffer boundary conditions differently.

variants.detail: every sub-block carries the maximum 255 payload bytes except possibly the last
variants.reason: What real encoders emit; the fewest sub-blocks for a given payload and the shortest framing overhead.

variants.detail: sub-blocks of 1-4 bytes each
variants.reason: Forces the decoder's sub-block loop to iterate many times over the same payload, which is where reassembly buffers and read-loop counters are exercised.

variants.detail: random sizes in 1-255 per sub-block, so boundaries do not align with anything
variants.reason: Breaks any decoder assumption that a sub-block boundary coincides with a code, row or record boundary - the LZW bitstream routinely spans sub-blocks.

variants.detail: exactly 1 byte, exactly 254, exactly 255, and single-sub-block payloads
variants.reason: The legal ends of the Size span, including the off-by-one neighbours of the 255 cap.

variants.detail: no payload sub-blocks at all, just the 0x00 terminator
variants.reason: Legal for comment, plain-text, application and unknown-extension data; reaches the zero-length-data path.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Framing overhead is 1 byte per sub-block, so tiny chunks add roughly 25% to a payload's byte cost while full 255-byte chunks add about 0.4%; that overhead is charged to the DATA output_budget. Note the empty-sequence variant is illegal for IMAGEDATA, whose payload must still deliver width*height pixel codes - it applies only to the extension data blocks.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose a chunking strategy per data block, weighted toward full and mixed chunks, with tiny chunks and empty sequences appearing regularly for extension data.
diversity_axes.notes: Whatever the chunking, Size must always equal the number of payload bytes actually written, and the sequence must always end with a 0x00 terminator.

diversity_axes.name: data
diversity_axes.why: The bytes inside a sub-block. For image data they are the LZW stream, whose content is free within a well-formed framing; for comment, plain-text, application and unknown-extension data they are arbitrary. Free in every case and never pinned.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: For image data, the LZW codes themselves; for text and application data, the byte values a decoder parses or skips. Random content maximises distinct decoder inputs at zero size cost.

variants.detail: inside image data: codes from a well-formed LZW encoder
variants.reason: The only case where content is constrained, and it is constrained by IMAGEDATA.LZWMinimumCodeSize and the pixel budget, not by this byte run.

variants.detail: uniform random content
variants.reason: Free for comment, plain-text, application and unknown-extension data; maximises distinct decoder inputs at zero size cost.

variants.detail: ASCII runs for comment and plain-text data
variants.reason: Reaches the text-parsing and text-rendering paths rather than the skip path.

variants.detail: bytes that mimic a block introducer or terminator
variants.reason: Proves the sub-block framing is what delimits data, not its content.

Note the empty-sequence variant is illegal for IMAGEDATA, whose payload must still deliver width*height pixel codes - it applies only to the extension data blocks.

diversity_axes.name: graphiccontrolextension_datasubblock_packedfields_reserved

diversity_axes.decoder_paths: None - masked out by conforming decoders; varying them confirms the mask is applied and diversifies the byte.

variants.detail: all three reserved bits clear, as real encoders write
variants.reason: The conventional value; the packed byte then matches every file a decoder has seen.

variants.detail: any value 1-7 in bits 7-5 of the packed byte
variants.reason: Reaches whatever a decoder does with reserved bits it was told to ignore; some mask them, some shift the whole byte.

diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 0 most of the time and a nonzero value in a minority of Graphic Control Extensions, independently of the disposal, user-input and transparency bits.
diversity_axes.notes: Recorded separately from image_reserved_bits because it lives in a different struct and a different packed byte.

diversity_axes.name: disposal_method
diversity_axes.why: A 3-bit enumeration with eight legal values, four named by GIF89a and four reserved-but-accepted; every one must be emitted because each is a distinct compositing branch, including the ones a decoder handles badly.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0 unspecified (decoder choice), 1 do-not-dispose (leave the frame in place), 2 restore-to-background (clear the frame rectangle to BackgroundColorIndex), 3 restore-to-previous (save and restore the canvas), 4-7 undefined and treated by most decoders as 0 or 1 - four separate paths through the frame-compositing state machine.

variants.detail: no disposal specified - the decoder decides
variants.reason: The default in files that omit the extension's semantics; reaches the implementation-defined path.

variants.detail: do not dispose - leave the graphic in place
variants.reason: The common animation case: frames accumulate on the canvas, so the compositor's copy-through path runs.

variants.detail: restore to background color
variants.reason: Makes BackgroundColorIndex semantically live and drives the clear-region-to-background code.

variants.detail: restore to previous
variants.reason: The deepest compositing path: the decoder must save and restore a frame buffer around the graphic.

variants.detail: reserved for future use
variants.reason: Legal 3-bit value that GIF89a leaves undefined; conforming decoders normalise or ignore it, so this reaches their clamping branch (Firefox clamps above 3, giflib stores the raw value).

variants.detail: reserved for future use
variants.reason: Same undefined-but-legal branch as 4; distinct raw value for decoders that store it.

variants.detail: reserved for future use
variants.reason: Same undefined-but-legal branch.

variants.detail: reserved for future use - the top of the 3-bit span
variants.reason: Completes the exhaustive legal set and is the value most likely to trip an unmasked shift.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - three bits inside an already-emitted byte; no size consequence, so all eight values are free to emit as often as wanted.
diversity_axes.how_varied: must_emit_full_legal_set: every value 0-7 must appear across a corpus. Weight 1, 2 and 3 most heavily because they drive the real compositing branches, but never drop 0 or 4-7.
diversity_axes.notes: Combine deliberately with DelayTime and UserInputFlag values, and with DisposalMethod 2 files that carry a nonzero BackgroundColorIndex, so the restore path has something to restore to.

diversity_axes.name: user_input_flag
diversity_axes.why: Both values are legal and both must be emitted; it costs nothing and selects a real branch in decoders that model user-input waiting.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 1 asks the decoder to wait for input before advancing the animation, which in library decoders selects the waiting-for-input state and its delay handling; 0 is the normal timed advance.

variants.detail: do not wait for user input
variants.reason: The default in every real animation; the frame advances on its delay alone.

variants.detail: wait for user input before continuing, bounded by DelayTime
variants.reason: Reaches the renderer's input-wait logic, a branch no other field can trigger.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - one bit inside an already-emitted byte; no size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: must_emit_full_legal_set: both values must appear across a corpus, with 0 dominant and 1 emitted regularly.
diversity_axes.notes: Semantically paired with DelayTime (the wait is bounded by the delay), so vary the two together rather than independently when covering that interaction.

diversity_axes.name: transparent_color_flag
diversity_axes.why: Both values must be emitted: transparency is the reason most real GIFs carry this extension at all, and dropping either 0 or 1 removes the transparency test or the opaque blit path.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 1 makes the decoder compare every decoded index against TransparentColorIndex and skip matching pixels (the alpha and compositing path); 0 takes the plain opaque blit.

variants.detail: no transparent colour; TransparentColorIndex is ignored
variants.reason: The default opaque path, and the one real static images use.

variants.detail: transparent colour present at TransparentColorIndex

diversity_axes.name: delay_time
diversity_axes.why: A centisecond delay the parser never validates; completely free, and worth varying because animation timing is one of the few places a decoder state machine sees different inputs.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0 means advance immediately and reaches the zero-delay fast path; small values are the normal timed path; 65535 and other extremes reach the delay-clamping and overflow handling in animation-aware decoders.

variants.detail: no delay - advance immediately

variants.detail: 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 hundredths of a second

variants.detail: 1, 2, 3 hundredths of a second

variants.detail: 10000, 60000, 65535 hundredths of a second

variants.detail: any ushort 0-65535

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - two bytes whatever the value; free to vary with no file-size consequence, so it should differ across frames within a file.

diversity_axes.name: transparent_color_index
diversity_axes.why: Free across 0..255 and never checked against the table size; listed because an author might pin it to 0, which would collapse the transparency comparison to a single index.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The index compared against every decoded pixel; an in-range value makes real pixels transparent, an out-of-range value reaches the no-pixel-matches path, and a value equal to the background index interacts with disposal method 2.

variants.detail: first palette entry transparent
variants.reason: The most common real-world choice.

variants.detail: any index below the active colour table's entry count, e.g. 1, 63, 255
variants.reason: Makes matching pixels actually vanish during compositing, exercising the transparency blit path with real data.

variants.detail: an index at or above the active table's entry count, e.g. 200 with a 4-colour table
variants.reason: Reaches the decoder's no-match path: the transparency test never fires, which is distinct from a matching index and from the flag being clear.

variants.detail: an index the LZW stream deliberately emits for some pixels (pair with the varied-indices payload shape)
variants.reason: Guarantees the transparency branch executes with matching pixels rather than by luck.

variants.detail: any value while TransparentColorFlag is 0
variants.reason: The index is unread in that case; varying it proves the decoder honours the flag rather than the index.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - one byte whatever the value; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw from 0-255 biased toward 0 and in-range values, always emitting out-of-range values in a minority of files; when TransparentColorFlag is 1, prefer indices the payload actually emits.
diversity_axes.notes: Never validated against the colour table size, which is exactly why out-of-range values are kept in the corpus.

diversity_axes.name: comment_data
diversity_axes.why: Arbitrary text in sub-blocks; completely free and the cheapest large diversity source in the format, so it must vary in length and content on every file.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The comment sub-block loop iteration count and the bytes a decoder either stores or skips; empty, one-byte, 255-byte and multi-block comments all take different loop paths.

variants.detail: no payload sub-blocks, just the 0x00 terminator
variants.reason: Cheapest legal comment; reaches the decoder's zero-length-skip path.

variants.detail: a few printable bytes, e.g. 'Created with FormatFuzzer'
variants.reason: What real encoders write; the common metadata path.

variants.detail: several hundred bytes spanning multiple 255-byte sub-blocks
variants.reason: Forces the comment skip loop to iterate across sub-block boundaries.

variants.detail: non-text bytes including 0x00, 0xFF and high-bit sequences
variants.reason: Comments are not required to be text; raw bytes reach whatever a decoder does when it tries to interpret or log them as a string.

variants.detail: thousands of bytes across many sub-blocks
variants.reason: Large skipped regions, which stress buffer reallocation inside the skip loop; charged to the DATA output_budget.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential: comment bytes count against the DATA output_budget like any other block (1 byte of framing per sub-block plus the payload). Long comments are therefore rare in a budget-bounded corpus, but the variant is never removed from the axis - the budget is met by emitting fewer other blocks.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose a variant per Comment Extension, weighted toward empty and short ASCII; only the sub-block framing is constrained, never the bytes inside it.
diversity_axes.notes: A comment is skipped by every conforming decoder, so its content cannot make a file invalid - which is exactly why it is a free Tier C axis.

diversity_axes.name: plain_text_data
diversity_axes.why: Free text bytes in sub-blocks; length and content vary with no validity consequence, so it must never be pinned to a fixed string.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The plain-text sub-block loop and, in decoders that render text, the character layout loop; length changes how many characters are laid out and can exceed the declared grid.

variants.detail: no payload sub-blocks, just the 0x00 terminator
variants.reason: Legal; reaches the decoder's zero-length text path.

variants.detail: exactly as many characters as the grid capacity implies (TextGridWidth/CharacterCellWidth * TextGridHeight/CharacterCellHeight)
variants.reason: The well-behaved case a text-rendering decoder expects.

variants.detail: fewer characters than the grid holds
variants.reason: Reaches the decoder's padding or partial-fill path.

variants.detail: more characters than the grid holds, so the renderer must wrap, clip or ignore the excess
variants.reason: Drives the wrap/clip logic and the row-advance boundary in text-rendering decoders.

variants.detail: control characters, 0x00, high-bit bytes
variants.reason: GIF89a does not restrict the character set; raw bytes reach whatever glyph lookup a decoder performs.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential: text bytes count against the DATA output_budget (1 framing byte per sub-block plus payload). Keeping text modest - tens of bytes - leaves room for images inside the same budget.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose a variant per Plain Text Extension and vary it together with plain_text_grid and plain_text_cell so the character count and the grid capacity disagree in the intended direction.
diversity_axes.notes: No dependency requires the character count to match grid capacity, so under-full and over-full text are both legal emissions.

diversity_axes.name: text_grid_left_position
diversity_axes.why: Text-grid origin, free across the ushort span; not tied to the canvas, because a decoder that renders text clips the grid exactly as it clips an image.

variants.detail: offset plus grid width exceeds the canvas

variants.detail: the top of the ushort span
variants.reason: Fully off-canvas grid; reaches the discard-without-rendering path.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - eight bytes total whatever the values; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of the other three grid coordinates across the full ushort span, weighted toward origin and in-canvas placements.

diversity_axes.name: text_grid_top_position
diversity_axes.why: Text-grid vertical origin, free across the ushort span for the same reason as the horizontal origin.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The text grid top origin and its clipping; values below the canvas reach the clipped-row path.

variants.detail: grid starts at the top of the canvas
variants.reason: The conventional origin.

variants.detail: a nonzero offset that leaves room for the grid
variants.reason: Reaches the offset row-start path of a text renderer.

variants.detail: the top of the ushort span

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - eight bytes total whatever the values; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of the other three grid coordinates across the full ushort span, weighted toward origin and in-canvas placements.
diversity_axes.notes: The grid is never validated against the logical screen size or against the character count, so all four variants are legal.

diversity_axes.name: text_grid_width
diversity_axes.why: A character count a size-conscious author would be tempted to pin; it is free, and the number of characters a text renderer lays out is derived from it, never the reverse.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The text grid column count and the wrap and clip behaviour of the character layout loop; 0 and very large values reach the degenerate and clipped branches.

variants.detail: as many character columns as the canvas and cell width allow
variants.reason: The largest grid a renderer will lay out without clipping.

variants.detail: a handful of columns
variants.reason: The common case; keeps the text data short so the file stays inside its budget.

variants.detail: zero columns
variants.reason: Degenerate grid; reaches the divide-by-cell-width and zero-column guard paths.

variants.detail: more columns than fit
variants.reason: Legal: the renderer wraps or clips, which is a distinct layout branch.

variants.detail: the top of the ushort span
variants.reason: Extreme column count; the character count a renderer derives from it.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - eight bytes total whatever the values; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of the other three grid coordinates across the full ushort span, weighted toward full-canvas and small-window layouts.
diversity_axes.notes: The grid is never validated against the logical screen size or against the character count, so all four variants are legal.

diversity_axes.name: text_grid_height
diversity_axes.why: The text grid row count, equally free and equally a count the renderer derives from rather than the other way round.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The text grid row count and the number of layout passes; with TextGridWidth it bounds how many characters a renderer consumes before stopping.

variants.detail: as many character rows as the canvas and cell height allow
variants.reason: The largest grid laid out without vertical clipping.

variants.detail: a handful of rows
variants.reason: The common case; bounds how many layout passes a renderer makes.

variants.detail: zero rows
variants.reason: Degenerate grid; reaches the zero-row guard path.

variants.detail: more rows than fit
variants.reason: Legal: rows below the canvas are clipped.

variants.detail: the top of the ushort span
variants.reason: Extreme row count; with TextGridWidth it bounds the character budget.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - eight bytes total whatever the values; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of the other three grid coordinates across the full ushort span, weighted toward full-canvas and small-window layouts.
diversity_axes.notes: The grid is never validated against the logical screen size or against the character count, so all four variants are legal.

diversity_axes.name: character_cell_width
diversity_axes.why: Free byte: the cell width a text renderer uses to advance characters. Pinning it would remove arithmetic variety for no depth.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The character advance width and the columns-per-grid computation; 0 reaches the degenerate divide-or-skip path and 255 the extreme-advance path.

variants.reason: The cell sizes real text modes use; gives cell counts a renderer lays out normally.
Maximises the computed cell count for a given grid, stressing the text layout loop.

variants.detail: cell dimensions exceeding TextGridWidth or TextGridHeight

diversity_axes.name: character_cell_height

diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The line advance and the rows-per-grid computation; 0 and 255 reach the degenerate and extreme paths of a text renderer.

variants.reason: The cell sizes real text modes use; gives cell counts a renderer lays out normally.
Maximises the computed cell count for a given grid, stressing the text layout loop.

variants.detail: cell dimensions exceeding TextGridWidth or TextGridHeight
variants.reason: Yields a zero-cell or single-cell grid after integer division - a distinct path from a zero cell dimension.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - two bytes whatever the values; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of CharacterCellWidth across 0-255, weighted toward the common text-mode sizes, and deliberately include zero and oversized cells in a minority of Plain Text Extensions.
diversity_axes.notes: These were close calls against Tier A: no Assert or comparison exists in the template and no conforming decoder refuses the file, so the divisor stays free.

diversity_axes.name: text_foreground_color_index
diversity_axes.why: A palette index for the text, never validated against the table size; free across 0..255.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The colour a text renderer draws with; an out-of-range value reaches the clamp-or-ignore path.

variants.detail: palette entry 0
variants.reason: The conventional choice and the entry the background index often shares.

variants.detail: an index the active table defines
variants.reason: The normal case: a real colour the renderer draws with.

variants.detail: an index beyond the active table size
variants.reason: Never validated, so it reaches the decoder clamp-or-ignore handling.

variants.detail: foreground equals TextBackgroundColorIndex
variants.reason: Invisible text; a legal degenerate case a renderer must still lay out.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - two bytes whatever the values; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of TextBackgroundColorIndex across 0-255, weighted toward in-range distinct values.
diversity_axes.notes: Never validated against the colour table size, so out-of-range values stay in the corpus.

diversity_axes.name: text_background_color_index
diversity_axes.why: The paired background palette index, free for the same reason.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The colour a text renderer fills behind the glyphs; out-of-range values reach the clamp-or-ignore path.

variants.detail: palette entry 0
variants.reason: The conventional choice.

variants.detail: an index the active table defines
variants.reason: The normal case: the cell fill colour.

diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw independently of TextForegroundColorIndex across 0-255, weighted toward in-range distinct values.
diversity_axes.notes: Never validated against the colour table size, so out-of-range values stay in the corpus.

diversity_axes.name: application_identifier
diversity_axes.why: Eight free bytes; the well-known NETSCAPE identifier is one point in that space, not a constraint on it, and the field must stay free so other identifiers are emitted too.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Decoders that dispatch on the identifier take the looping-extension path for NETSCAPE and the generic skip path for anything else; each distinct identifier is a separate string comparison.

variants.detail: the looping-extension identifier
variants.reason: The one identifier decoders actually dispatch on, so it must appear often.

variants.detail: identifiers other decoders recognise, e.g. MGKpg/89A
variants.reason: Reaches vendor-specific handlers in the decoders that have them.

variants.detail: eight arbitrary printable bytes
variants.reason: The generic path: the decoder compares, fails and skips the sub-blocks.

variants.detail: non-printable identifier bytes
variants.reason: Proves the field is a fixed-width byte run, not a string with validation.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - eleven fixed bytes whatever the content; the bytes are free and cost nothing extra, so the identifier should vary across a corpus.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit the NETSCAPE looping form regularly - it is the only identifier with real semantic effect - and fill the rest with other known, unknown printable and binary identifiers.
diversity_axes.notes: No decoder rejects an unrecognised identifier, which is why the full 8+3 byte space stays free rather than being pinned to 'NETSCAPE'/'2.0'.

diversity_axes.name: application_authentication_code
diversity_axes.why: Three free bytes paired with the identifier; 2.0 is the de-facto value for NETSCAPE but the field itself is unconstrained and must vary.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The second string comparison in the application dispatch; a code that does not match the identifier reaches the unknown-application-data path.

variants.detail: the de-facto code paired with NETSCAPE
variants.reason: What makes the looping extension recognisable to real decoders.

variants.detail: three arbitrary printable bytes
variants.reason: Reaches the unknown-application-data path.

variants.detail: non-printable code bytes
variants.reason: The field is an unchecked byte run, so any content is legal.

variants.detail: a code that does not belong to the identifier
variants.reason: Legal and unvalidated; decoders that check the pair reach their mismatch branch.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - eleven fixed bytes whatever the content; the bytes are free and cost nothing extra, so the identifier should vary across a corpus.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 2.0 whenever the identifier is NETSCAPE, and otherwise vary the three bytes freely, including codes that do not match the identifier they accompany.
diversity_axes.notes: No decoder rejects an unrecognised identifier, which is why the full 8+3 byte space stays free rather than being pinned to 'NETSCAPE'/'2.0'.

diversity_axes.name: application_data
diversity_axes.why: Free sub-block payload: for NETSCAPE it carries the looping count, for anything else arbitrary bytes. Both length and content vary.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The application sub-block loop; for the looping extension the two data bytes are parsed as an iteration count (0 meaning loop forever), which is a distinct branch from skipping unrecognised application data.

variants.detail: no payload sub-blocks, just the 0x00 terminator
variants.reason: Legal and cheap; reaches the decoder's zero-length skip path.

variants.detail: [0x03][0x01][little-endian ushort loop count], with counts 0 (infinite), 1, 2, 65535
variants.reason: The de-facto Netscape payload; the loop-count value itself selects the infinite-loop and finite-loop branches.

variants.detail: a handful of random bytes in one sub-block
variants.reason: Generic unrecognised application data, the most common real case.

variants.detail: hundreds of bytes spanning several sub-blocks
variants.reason: Forces the application-data skip loop to cross sub-block boundaries.

variants.detail: loop record with a wrong sub-block length (not 0x03) or a wrong sub-block identifier (not 0x01)
variants.reason: Reaches the validation branch inside a decoder's Netscape handling rather than its loop-count branch.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential: application bytes count against the DATA output_budget (1 framing byte per sub-block plus payload). The loop record costs 5 bytes, so it is essentially free and should appear often.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose per Application Extension, weighted toward the loop record and short arbitrary data; only the sub-block framing is constrained, never the bytes inside.
diversity_axes.notes: Content is application-defined by specification, so nothing here can make the file invalid - the framing constraints in structure are what keep it parseable.

diversity_axes.name: label
diversity_axes.why: The template else-branch accepts any label that is not one of the four it dispatches on, so the legal set is every byte except 0x01, 0xF9, 0xFE and 0xFF, and no member of it may be dropped from a corpus.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each distinct label is a separate comparison in the extension dispatch chain and lands in the generic unknown-extension handler; labels a specific decoder does recognise (vendor extensions) reach that decoder own handler.

variants.reason: Labels below every defined one; reaches the decoder's dispatch fall-through with small values.
High-bit labels, which distinguishes signed-char from unsigned-char comparisons in decoders written in C.

variants.detail: 0x00 and 0x02 around Plain Text 0x01; 0xF8 and 0xFA around Graphic Control 0xF9; 0xFD and 0xFF-excluded neighbours around Comment 0xFE; 0xFE and 0xFF-excluded neighbours around Application 0xFF
variants.reason: Off-by-one label values are the classic place a dispatch table or range check misfires; they still route to the generic skip because the four defined labels are excluded from this axis.

variants.detail: 0xFF is excluded here, so 0xFE is excluded too - the largest legal value on this axis is 0xFD
variants.reason: Top of the legal span for an unrecognised label.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: n/a - one byte whatever the value; free to vary with no file-size consequence.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Draw uniformly from the 252 legal bytes, with extra weight on the neighbours of the four defined labels; never emit 0x01, 0xF9, 0xFE or 0xFF in this position, since those select a different block form.
diversity_axes.notes: must_emit_full_legal_set applies with an exclusion list: the legal set is every byte except {0x01, 0xF9, 0xFE, 0xFF}, and no member of that set may be dropped from a corpus. The template's stale '// F9' comment on line 195 is not a required value.

diversity_axes.name: undefineddata_data_sub_blocks
diversity_axes.why: Free bytes in sub-block framing; length and content vary and this is the place to carry arbitrary data without affecting validity.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The unknown-extension sub-block loop and the skip path; length changes the loop iteration count and the number of bytes a decoder must skip to resynchronise on the next block.

variants.detail: no payload sub-blocks, just the 0x00 terminator - a 4-byte extension in total
variants.reason: The cheapest way to make a decoder take and leave its unknown-extension skip path, so many can fit inside one output_budget.

variants.detail: a few random bytes in one sub-block
variants.reason: The common shape for private extensions; exercises resynchronisation onto the next block.

variants.detail: hundreds of bytes spanning several sub-blocks
variants.reason: Forces the skip loop to iterate across sub-block boundaries before resynchronising.

variants.detail: payload bytes containing 0x2C, 0x21 and 0x3B values, and even the ASCII text 'GIF89a'
variants.reason: Proves the decoder skips by length rather than by scanning for markers; a naive skipper will desynchronise here.

variants.detail: thousands of bytes across many sub-blocks
variants.reason: Large skipped regions stress buffer growth inside the skip loop; charged to the DATA output_budget.

diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Consequential: these bytes count against the DATA output_budget like every other block. Because unknown extensions are the cheapest depth per byte when empty (4 bytes total), they are an efficient way to spend budget on skip-path coverage rather than on image data.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Choose per unknown extension, weighted toward empty and short random; only the sub-block framing is constrained, never the payload bytes.
diversity_axes.notes: Unknown extensions are valuable precisely because every conforming decoder must skip them correctly and continue parsing - a desynchronising skip shows up as a failure on the following block.
